*Tārābhaktisudhārṇavaḥ* (The Ocean of Nectar of Devotion to Tārā).
Composed by the Great Preceptor, the Illustrious Narasimha Thakkura, [for] the most eminent scholar...
Edited by Śrī Pañcānana Tarka-Sāṃkhya-Vedāntatīrtha, Tantrik Texts Series,
Calcutta, 1934.
Oṃ,
homage to Nīlasarasvatī; [this is] the Ocean of the Nectar of Devotion to Tārā.
First Wave:
The Auspicious Invocation.
[I bow to the one] whose splendor is as delightful as a village of clouds, skillful at the rain of jewels from the nose of the plow-wielder (Indra).

I joyfully worship a certain honey-bee situated within the lotus of my heart— resplendent with the pollen arising from the single veil of his two dancing yellow garments, and possessing a deep, steady resonance shimmering under the pretext of playing the flute.

I bow to Aparṇā, who stands firm as a pillar; whose flowers shine with the pretext of her smiles, whose breasts are her silver fruits, who is swarmed by rows of intoxicated bees under the guise of her rising locks of hair, and who is rendered childless by the beautiful anklets she wears.
I bow to a certain graceful wish-fulfilling creeper that has sprung from the king of mountains.
By touching the surface of the forehead, it assumes the nature of the crescent moon;
by settling upon the hair, it takes on the form of the Ganges;
and it always shines within the hearts of the virtuous in the essence of the Kaustubha gem.
Salutation to that incomparable one, the dust of the feet of the Guru.
Having mastered various tantras from the mouth of his preceptor Gadādhara,
this Narasiṃha composes the *Tārābhaktisudhārṇava*.

Even though I have scrutinized the words composed by Śambhu, does my skill not shine forth before other people? [It is like this: among great jewels produced in the midst of the ocean, what comparison can there be with those found on the shore?
Is the attribution of qualities to those who possess them anything but a source of wonder?
p. 2) Praise of Knowledge:
In the Rudrayāmala, Śrī Mahādeva said: "O beloved of Hara, tell me what is to be said beyond this."
Pārvatī said:
"O Mahādeva, tell me the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), which is dear to me.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
O Great Goddess, when all was destroyed and both the mobile and immobile had perished,
there arose before creation a single, vast, and most great cosmic egg.
There, Viṣṇu himself was born, endowed with four arms;
Hari held a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus in his four hands.
Then, at the destruction of that which was created, Brahmā was born from his navel;
and from the region of his forehead, Hara himself was born as Rudra.
Brahmā questioned Viṣṇu, the Lord of Gods and liberator from the three worlds:
"By propitiating which knowledge is one called a knower of the four Vedas?"
Viṣṇu said: "Ask Hara, the Lord of Gods, Śaṅkara.
(Sarasvatī, the Great Knowledge, is established within the body of Śiva.
Having heard those words of his, Brahmā questioned Śaṅkara.
O Lord of Gods, tell us of her by the name Nīlasarasvatī.
Having heard the words of Brahmā, Maheśvara laughed and said:
"Listen attentively, O Brahmin, to the knowledge of Nīlasarasvatī;
having obtained her grace, you shall speak the four Vedas."
In the western region of Meru, there is a lake known by the name Cola;
there, Nīlasarasvatī herself, the mother of the Vedas, was born.
At that very time, however, he who was intent upon the peak of Mount Meru,
having completed his recitation of the mantra three times over three ages, remained there.
Emerging from my upward-facing mouth as a mass of radiant energy,
it descended into the ocean and formerly became blue in color.
Then, on the northern part of the lake, there was a certain sage;
Śiva, assuming the guise of a muni, took up residence there under the name Akṣobhya.
At that very time, the goddess Pārvatī, naturally beautiful, seated upon the chest of the Lord of Gods who was staying on the peak of Kailāsa, the daughter of the mountain, questioned him.
O Lord, how did those whose wealth was their penance obtain omniscience?
Having acquired what knowledge did the sages compose the *Bhārata* and other works?
Having heard the words of the daughter of the mountain, the Supreme Lord smiled and, embracing his beloved, spoke while honoring her, saying, "Excellent! Excellent!"
Listen, O virtuous lady, to this Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) which burns the fuel of ignorance,
having attained which the great-souled ones composed the Mahābhārata and other works.
The poets of pure intellect considered nothing to be impossible;
for in debate within the assembly, there was that [speech] which paralyzed the words of their opponents.
She who brings about the destruction of great enmity for the wise through the offering of oblations,
yet speaks even impure things to the laughter of men.
One may bring even a disputant, a king, or a minister under one's control;
through the mere knowledge of the mantra and by its recitation, one shall attain omniscience.
By merely placing [the mantra] upon the tongue, even a mute becomes a skilled poet;
a wretched person becomes wealthy, and a king attains sovereignty.
By the grace of this mantra, a Brahmin attains liberation.
Listen, O Maheśānī: one should never give [this] to a Śūdra;
[for him] the intellect would not be unimpeded in the scripture, like the victory of Vākpati.
In the Phetkāriṇī Tantra,
the Daughter of the Mountain questioned Him who was seated on the peak of Kailāsa, adorned with a crescent moon, while she sat upon His chest.
O Lord, how did those whose wealth is penance obtain omniscience?
Having acquired what knowledge did the sages compose the *Bhārata* and other works?
Having heard the words of the daughter of the mountain, the Supreme Lord laughed and, embracing his beloved, spoke while honoring her, saying, "Excellent! Excellent!"
Listen, O virtuous lady, to this Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) which burns the fuel of ignorance;
having attained it, great-souled beings [succeed] in the realms of dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation.
The poets of pure intellect considered nothing to be impossible;
for in debate within the assembly, their words were capable of paralyzing their opponents.
4) O Goddess, she causes the loss of knowledge for the learned by offering oblations;
she who speaks even what is impure for the amusement of the members of the assembly.
One may bring even a disputant, a king, or a minister under one's control;
merely by knowing this mantra and reciting it, one may attain omniscience.
The grammatical connection is that one should cause the opponent to speak.
Likewise, the Tārā mantra is as follows:
Having first given the letter *sa* together with its vowel, adorned with the fourth vowel (*ū*),
mounted upon the letter *ra*, radiant and throbbing, and endowed with the lunar drop (*bindu*).
Then one should give the syllable *traṃ*, adorned with the fourth vowel;
thereafter, one should join the letter *ha* conjoined with the long vowel *ū*.

Then one should utter the syllable *phaṭ*; thus the mantra is complete and perfected. [The seed-syllable is formed as follows: the letter *ha* with the fourth vowel *ī*, the moon which is the half-moon (*ardhacandra*), and the bindu which is the anusvāra; joined with the long vowel *ū*, the letter *ha* becomes *hūṃ*.
In the Matsyasūkta:
Now I shall declare the unsurpassed extraction of the mantra of the Great Goddess,
knowing which a man shines like another Vācaspati.
Having extracted the seed-syllable of Māyā (Hrīṃ) and likewise the first letter of the dental class (ta),
conjoined with Rati (ī), Bindu (m), and Fire (ra), one obtains the second, most excellent seed-syllable.
The third is the seed-syllable of the *kūrca*, followed by the syllable *phaṭ*;
this is the complete perfected mantra, endowed with the five rays of light.

The seed-syllable of Māyā is *hrīṃ*. The first letter of the dental class (*tavarga*) is *ta*. *Rati* is the vowel *ī*. The dot is the *anusvāra*. *Vahni* is the letter *ra*; thus, [the syllable] is *trīṃ*. The seed-syllable of Kūrca is *hūṃ*. The five-rayed *oṃkāra* is *oṃ*. Having extracted the unsurpassed [syllable] from the ocean of stars (*tārārṇava*), that which follows Māyā is supreme.
Associated with the absence of conceptual proliferation (papañca), it is proclaimed as having five rays of light.
O Goddess, the mantra revealed is as follows: first *jīvanī*, then *madhyagā*, followed by *ekākṣī*, and after that *ugraṃ* and *darpaṃ*.

The syllable *a* is the Unsurpassed (*anuttara*). The syllable *ū* is the Supreme Illusion (*māyottama*). The syllable *ma* is the End of Proliferation (*papañcama*). *Hrīṃ* is Jīvanī. *Trīṃ* is Ekākṣī. *Hūṃ* is Ugrā. *Phaṭ* is Darpā. For the awakening to reality:
*Tāraṃ*, *Lajjāṃ*, *Traṃ*, Kāmeśī, *Hūṃ Phaṭ*—this is Ugratārikā.
One should worship Ekajaṭā with the mantra "Māyā trīṃ hūm" ending with the weapon-mantra (phaṭ).
One should designate this [mantra] as being devoid of the weapon-syllable by means of Nīlasarasvatī.
Kāmeśī is the syllable *ī*.
This great three-syllabled mantra, ending with *phaṭ*, resides in the heart.
Endowed with five rays of light, it then burns the fuel of ignorance.
In the *Tantracūḍāmaṇi*:
"This Great Vidyā ends with the weapon-mantra (*astra*); she who bears the mass of matted hair, when joined with the beginning of the Vedas at her mouth, is Tārā, the savior from the three worlds."
In the Matsyasūkta:
"Because she bestows speech through her divine play, she is Nīlasarasvatī;
because she always delivers [beings] across [samsara], she is Tārā, the bestower of happiness and liberation."
Because she delivers from fierce calamities, Ugratārā is so proclaimed;
likewise:
the seed-syllable of modesty (hrīḥ), the seed-syllable of the bride (strī), the seed-syllable of the tuft (kūrcabīja), and likewise phaṭ.
Thus, the five-syllabled vidyā reveals the five elements; likewise,
the three-syllabled Mahānīlasarasvatī is devoid of the Tārā-weapon mantra.
It is known as Kullukā and is concealed within the three worlds.
In that very place, a most terrible curse was also pronounced by the sage Vasiṣṭha.
From that time forward, this vidyā has not been fruitful for anyone;
it is the seed-syllable of Śakti joined above the seed-syllable situated within Trapā.
From that time forth, this science has been like a glorious bride.

The seed-syllable of power (śakti-bīja) is the letter *sa*. The seed-syllable of modesty (*trapā*) consisting of the inner semi-vowels is the syllable *trīṃ*. By these, the word *strī* is established.
Also, in the *Tārārṇava*:
Furthermore, because this fierce [vidyā] was propitiated by Vasiṣṭha and does not yield fruit quickly,
for that reason a most terrible curse was pronounced by that sage as well;
from that time forward, this vidyā has not granted its fruit to anyone.
The seed-syllable of Śakti is joined above the seed-syllable situated within Trapā;
from that point onward, this Vidyā is illustrious like a bride.
This lore is the fruit-bearer of all sciences, the victorious for those desiring victory;
it is the knowledge that destroys poison and bestows immortality.
By the mere knowledge of the mantra, one becomes victorious on earth;
even a mute becomes a lord of speech, and the man becomes like Bṛhaspati.
Therefore, it is said in the *Tantracūḍāmaṇi*:
"Just as the word 'new bride' causes pain to the husband,
so too this Great Vidyā never comes within the range of the Kula."
Thus, by the word *vadhū*, the second seed-syllable (*bīja*) indeed comes forth joined with the letter *sa*.
However, once the incarnation of Kṛṣṇa has occurred, she is released from the curse once again.
According to the statement in another tantra, "The curse lasts only until the incarnation of Kṛṣṇa"—this is the essential truth.
In the Matsyasūkta:
"When the Vidya begins with the Śrī-bīja, then Śrī is manifest in every direction;
indeed, this same Mahāvidyā, when preceded by Māyā, grants all desired objects."
She whose beginning is the Vāgbhava syllable is the embodiment of the Great Sayings (mahāvākya) and consists of all speech.
Likewise: "The accomplishment of the pill (guṭikā), the Vetāla, the Pātāla, the Vaṭayakṣiṇī, entry into another's body, and the accomplishment of the Command (ājñāsiddhi) are produced."
Merely by contemplating [the mantra] on the tongue, one will certainly become a knower of the three times;
that best of practitioners who contemplates the Vidyā without making any distinction [between them].
He who is liberated while living (jīvanmukta) shall certainly become fully liberated at the end.
As stated in the *Brahmasaṃhitā*: "Other mantras, even when mastered, may yield all their fruits;
however, this mantra yields its fruit merely upon being received, even if it has not been mastered."
In the *Phetkāriṇī*: "Nīlasarasvatī, who is always well-disposed toward the worlds, will, through my power, become especially so in the Kali age."
When a practitioner who has mastered the mantra places his hand upon the head of even a child,
he quickly instructs him, and that child, moreover, recites verses.
He instructs him, commanding, "Compose a verse.
Even one of little knowledge, if eloquent, the learned will honor;
behold the astrologer, who, though marvelous like Vācaspati himself, is held in high esteem.
By the mere knowledge of the mantra, two powers arise:
instantaneous poetic inspiration and invincibility against others.
Likewise: "On the day one obtains this mantra, there shall be gain therein;
one certainly obtains a sign (*pratyaya*) regarding both good and bad karma.
*Pratyaya* here means destruction. "Regarding both good and bad karma" refers to merit and demerit. Furthermore:
Thus has this manifestation been shown by Nīlasarasvatī;
it was first told to us by Brahmā, and now by me to you, O daughter of the mountain.
In the mantra of Nīlasarasvatī, which removes obstacles to poetic composition,
lack of resolve is the third [obstacle], but there is nothing else that causes an obstacle.

Regarding the phrase "obstructing poetic composition": it means that for one who is intent on poetry characterized by extraordinary wonder, and who is prone to indolence regarding spiritual practice, there will be no effort toward the great supernatural powers such as *aṇimā* and the rest.
Thus ends the first wave in the *Tārābhaktisudhārṇava* composed by the Great Mahopādhyāya Thakkura Śrī Narasiṃha. || 1 ||
The second wave:
The rules for receiving the mantra,
according to the *Mahogratārākalpa*.
If a person sees Tārā on her own during the Kalpa and seizes her,
no atonement is prescribed even for thousands of Manvantaras.
One should receive the sin-destroying Mahāvidyā from the mouth of a Guru.
In the Mahākālasaṃhitā:
"One should not speak after merely looking at a scripture, nor act upon it, nor even recite it;
one should not look [at it], nor teach it, nor perform it, nor indeed accomplish its goals."
Having obtained the recitation, ritual placement, worship, and so forth from the instruction of the guru,
one should thereafter accomplish all of that, always permeated by that state of being.
Now, regarding the characteristics of the Guru, the *Tantracūḍāmaṇi* states: "One who is of noble lineage is proclaimed to be qualified for all sciences;
he alone is the master of initiation here for every mantra, and no other."
Regarding the one of noble lineage (*kulīna*), it is stated in the *Kulārṇava*:
"He who knows the reality of the Kula, who is proficient in the Kula scriptures, and who is devoted to the worship of the Kula—he shall be a true Kaulika; any other is a hypocrite."

He who is pleased upon seeing those devoted to the lineage, who follow the conduct of the lineage, who possess the knowledge of the lineage, and who observe the vows of the lineage— he, the Kaulika, is dear to me.
One who knows the reality of the meaning of the root mantra, which is based on the acceptance of the three principles,
and who is devoted to the deity and the guru, shall indeed become a Kaulika through initiation.
But the *paśu* has no authority.
The *paśu*, however, is of two kinds: the divine (*deva*) and the former (*pūrva*), namely Bhairava.
His authority lies in worship, never in the state of a guru.

Thus, from the words of the Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi: "There are two kinds [of people] who revile the Kula conduct—the reviler and the non-reviler. This refers specifically to those who have received the Śākta initiation. Regarding the characteristics of the Guru, it is stated in the Kulārṇava:
"O Supreme Goddess, the venerable Guru is one whose dress is pure and who is captivating to the mind."
Endowed with all the primary marks and beautified by all the secondary characteristics.
He knows the true meaning of all scriptures, he is conversant with the application of all mantras,
he causes the delusion of the world, and his appearance is as pleasing as that of a god.

He has a pleasant countenance, is easy to approach, is transparently clear, possesses a pure inner nature, and has severed all doubt; he discerns through gestures, facial expressions, and movements, and has kept the very wicked at a distance.
Inward-turned yet outward-looking, omniscient, and knowing the proper place and time; perfected through command, knowing the three times, and capable of both restraint and grace.
One who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāntas, who is tranquil, who is devoted to compassion for all living beings,
whose movement of the senses is self-governed, and who is capable of conquering the sixfold group [of internal enemies].
Foremost among the assembly, exceedingly profound, a knower of the distinction between worthy and unworthy recipients,
stainless, eternally contented, free from dualities, and possessed of constant power.
Affectionate toward true devotees, steadfast, compassionate, and one whose speech is preceded by a smile;
fond of devotion, impartial toward all, merciful, and a teacher of disciples.
Eager to worship his chosen deity, his preceptor, and wise women, he is devoted to blameless actions— whether they be daily, occasional, or performed for specific desires.
Free from attachment, aversion, fear, anger, deceit, and egoism,
he is devoted to the practice of his own knowledge and is an illuminator of the sciences.
Content with whatever comes by chance, discerning between virtues and faults,
unattached to women, wealth, and the like, and abandoned by the vice of bad company;
One who is free from greed, non-violent, impartial, and discerning;
one who does not sell mantras, yantras, tantras, and the like for the sake of wealth, learning, or other such motives.
Free from conceptualization, free from discursive thought, having ascertained the Self, and exceedingly righteous;
equal toward blame and praise, observing silence, indifferent, and self-restrained.
O beloved, the Śrī Guru is said to be endowed with such characteristics as these:
he is pure-hearted, compassionate, a Brāhmaṇa, and one who has mastered the Vedas.
Always devoted to the conduct of his lineage, he applies himself to the scriptures of his family;
he is peaceful, self-controlled, all-knowing, and free from greed and delusion.
Having abandoned anger and delusion, he is free from passion and honored by heroes;
he is a knower of the Nigamas and Āgamas, and his excellent mind is serene.
9) One who has renounced all stages of life and is intent upon the worship of women—
one endowed with such characteristics as these— should worship the Guru with reverence.
In the Mahākapila-pañcarātra:
"Neither too young nor too old, neither lame nor emaciated;
neither with extra limbs nor lacking limbs, neither bald nor with protruding teeth."
One who is grateful for favors, eloquent, brave, well-established, and has mastered the scriptures;
one who has practiced the science of architecture and is capable of discerning the extraction of splinters.
One who knows the sequence of ritual actions and discerns the *mudrā* tantras—[as stated] in the *Tattvasāra*: "One who eats excessively, procrastinates, and is greedy for sense objects;
one who delights in causal reasoning, is wicked, a mere talker, and a reviler of the guru."
Aroma, Bahuroma, Nindita-āśramasevaka, Kāladanta, Asitoṣṭha, and Durgandhi-śvāsavāhaka.
Even if he is himself a lord,
a teacher who possesses wicked characteristics and is addicted to accepting many gifts brings about the destruction of prosperity.

In the *Ṣoḍaśārṇava*: "One who is childless, one whose children have died, a *kuṇḍa*, as well as a dwarf, one with deformed nails, one with black teeth, one conquered by women, and one with an extra limb."
One who is deficient in limbs, deceitful, diseased, talkative, or hunchbacked—
only he who is free from these defects is a true Guru, a vessel for the learned.

In the Vārāhītantra: "One should not appoint as a guru someone who bears one's own name, nor one whose wife bears the name of one's mother. Somaśambhu states: "A guru should be endowed with [proper] place, time, learning, conduct, behavior, character, and virtues; furthermore, he should be naturally perfected and appointed by a [legitimate] guru."
In the Vīrāgama: "A learned man born in a land situated between Kumārī and Himavat, which is naturally frequented by black deer, is indeed worthy of the status of an Ācārya."
In the *Śivapaddhati*: "The most excellent gurus are those born in Madhyadeśa, Kurukṣetra, Nābhī, and Ujjayinī, as well as those from Antarvedī, Pratiṣṭhāna, and Āvanti."
The Gauḍas, Śālvodbhavas, Sauras, Māgadhas,
Keralas, Kośalas, and Daśārṇas— these seven are the central Gurudeśas.
Those born in Karṇāṭa, Narmadārāṣṭra, Kaccha, and Ābhīra,
as well as the Kāliṅgas, the Kāmarūpas, and the Kāmbojas, are considered the lowest.
According to the Devīmata: "The preceptor is one who knows the Śaiva scriptures, born in a land sacred to Śiva;
he may be either a celibate student or a householder, and must be entirely devoted to devotion for Śiva. (10)
The preceptor is said to be one born under a lunar mansion favorable to the patron (*yajamāna*).
As stated in the *Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra*: "He should be a householder or established in celibacy (*brahmacarya*), and free from the eight letters beginning with 'ka'."
One should always make such a person one's teacher, who is devoted to the vows of fasting.
In the Śaiva Āgama: "O Maheśvarī, a householder seeking both enjoyment and liberation should not perform mantra-initiation for mendicants, forest-dwellers, or those belonging to the [other] castes."
Ascetics who have renounced the sacred fires, are devoid of ritual acts, and possess no belongings—
even if they dwell in the forest— are exactly like that [the liberated], because the student (brahmacārī) is one whose stage of life is still incomplete.
Therefore, O Maheśvarī, they have no authority for bestowing initiation;

nor, O beloved, should one seeking enjoyment and liberation choose ascetics (yatins), forest-dwellers (vaikhānasas), or likewise those still bound by caste-stages (varṇins) as gurus for initiation into the true nature of Śiva.
In the Yoginītantra: "Having received initiation from an ascetic (yati), if one is ever deluded, the expiation is either one cow or the three-night vow."
Having performed an expiation thereafter, one should undergo initiation once again.
As stated in the Rudrayāmala: "The initiation of a father, the initiation of an ascetic (yati), and the initiation of a forest-dweller..."
For one dwelling in a secluded hermitage, initiation destroys sons, longevity, and wealth.

In the *Siddhayāmala*: "O Dear One, if by the power of fortune one should obtain a perfected *vidyā*, then at that very moment one should be initiated into it, abandoning all deliberation regarding a guru."
But in the bestowing of one's own chosen vidyā, one should not entertain thoughts of a guru;
as stated in the Mohaśūrottara: "The mantra-practitioner, possessing knowledge, well-composed, and observing the vows of conduct regarding the phonemes..."
A renowned ascetic who is eternally devoted [to his practice], whether he be a householder or even a forest-dweller, may be a guru.
In this context, the statement regarding the weightiness of the ascetic refers to those other than householders. In the *Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra*:
"He whose supreme devotion to Viṣṇu is equal to his devotion to Viṣṇu himself—he alone is to be known as the true teacher; I tell you this truth."
In the *Nāradapañcarātra*: "A Brāhmaṇa who knows all times should bestow grace upon all;
in his absence, an excellent twice-born man who is peaceful in soul and absorbed in the Blessed One [should do so]."
Among those of the Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra castes, the Kṣatriya is capable of bestowing favor;
and even for a Kṣatriya, such [a person] may serve as a teacher in the absence of [another] guru.

The Vaiśya should perform it; thus, there should always be mutual assistance between the two. O Great-minded One, with a Śūdra of the same caste and similar status, the Śūdra’s favoring and consecration should always be performed. (11)

Furthermore, when a person of superior caste or a guru is present— whether he be renowned or not, and whether he resides in one's own country or elsewhere— one who desires auspiciousness should not perform this act.
But he who should act contrary to what exists—wherever that may be—will suffer ruin both in this world and the next; therefore, one should practice what is taught in the scriptures.

In the *Candrayāmala*: "One should not initiate those of the Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, or Śūdra castes in the reverse order [of the varṇas]. In the *Tantra*, it is stated by those expert in mantra: "The preceptor, the maternal uncle, the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*), the paternal uncle, the father-in-law, and the king—these six are also declared here to be gurus."
In the Jñānonnayana and Yoginītantra:
"Indeed, the mantra of a father, as well as that of a maternal grandfather,
of a younger brother, and of one who has taken the side of an enemy, is devoid of power."
In the Yoginītantra: "If one should perform the initiation of the father out of negligence or likewise through ignorance, one must then perform an expiation and undergo initiation once again."

Here, the genitive case in the word *pituḥ* (of the father) is used in the sense of disregard (*anādara*). Thus, the meaning is that if a lack of respect toward the father and others—manifested as devotion—should arise due to excessive familiarity and the like, then the mantra must not be received from the son or others. Even in that regard, Manu, having reflected, [stated] according to the *Prayogasāra*: "To a son endowed with devotion, or to one who gives wealth... and so forth.

It appears to me that [the mantra] should be given even to the eldest son if he is disciplined, based on statements from the *Phetkāriṇī* and other texts. However, some maintain that because of the statement in the *Phetkāriṇī* and elsewhere that "one should give it to the eldest son who is the ornament of his own family," only the eldest son who is devoted has the qualification to receive the mantra from his father.
Some say that [the initiation] is not [permissible] from the youngest son, nor from the maternal grandfather and others, nor for the daughter’s sons and so forth.

Others, however, based on the statement in the *Bhairava Tantra* that "one should not perform the mental contemplation of a guru during the instruction of one's own mantra," maintain that there is a prohibition against receiving [the mantra] from a father or other relatives by one who has not previously worshipped the mantra.
Thus they say. However, in the *Matsyasūkta*, it is stated:
"Indeed, a mantra devoid of power (*nirvīrya*) belonging to a father [of a different lineage] does not cause defect in the Śaiva or Śākta [traditions].
In the *Rudrayāmala*:
A husband shall not initiate his wife; a father shall not initiate his daughter;
likewise, a son shall not initiate [his father], nor shall a brother initiate his brother.
This too concerns only those who are not [proper] devotees. For this very reason:
"It was previously told by Brahmā to the high-souled Vasiṣṭha;
Vasiṣṭha himself also gave it to his own son, my father."

Thus, even the statement of the *Matsyasūkta* is consistent: "Receiving mantras from a woman is praiseworthy. This is because of the statement in the *Yoginītantra*: "Initiation by women is declared auspicious; that from one's mother is remembered as being eightfold [more effective]. However, she too is prohibited if she is a widow.
She was virtuous, of excellent conduct, devoted to her guru, and had conquered her senses;
she knew the true meaning and essence of all mantras, possessed good character, and delighted in worship.
"For she would be unfit as a guru, being devoid of a husband," as it is stated in that very same [text]. And in the *Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra*:
"The twice-born who perceives the Self as distinct from everything..."
Even if he is devoid of all auspicious marks, he is a guru; there is no doubt about this.
But one who has awakened through the Pañcarātra and knows the reality of the meaning of the Siddhānta is declared to be an Ācārya, even if he is devoid of all [other] characteristics.

In the Vaiśampāyana-saṃhitā: "That which is obtained in a dream or given by a woman is purified by means of a purificatory rite (saṃskāra) alone. And that purificatory rite is described in that very same work:
And one should cause the breaths of the Guru to enter a flask obtained in a dream;
having written [the mantra] with saffron on a banyan leaf, its reception is auspicious.
From that, one attains success; otherwise, it would be fruitless.

Regarding the Candra-pīṭha: "Mantras obtained in a dream, given by a woman, or given by anyone else—even if they have not been mastered—should nevertheless be received from a true guru, for they are indeed granters of results."

Thus ends the definition of the Guru; now, the definition of the disciple is given in the Kulārṇava: "O Mistress of the Kula, a true disciple is one who is endowed with all the auspicious characteristics."
Endowed with the means of practice such as tranquility, and possessed of virtuous qualities and moral discipline.
Born of a pure body and lineage, righteous, pure-minded,
firm in his vows, of virtuous conduct, and endowed with faith and devotion.
One who is grateful, fearful of evil, esteemed by the virtuous and the good,
a believer in the afterlife, generous by nature, and devoted to the welfare of all living beings.
Endowed with trustworthiness and humility, free from stinginess regarding wealth,
a achiever of the impossible, heroic, and possessed of strength and splendor.
One who acts with favor, is vigilant, and discerning;
who speaks what is beneficial, true, moderate, and affectionate, and is free from fault-finding.
13) One who grasps the meaning upon hearing it once, possesses keen intelligence and extensive wisdom;
one who remains unchanged whether on the ground, a bed, a seat, or in one's lap, and who requires no attendant.
A hero who acts with deliberation, free from the poverty of mind,
highly skilled in all undertakings, steadfast, and helpful to all.
O beloved, [I seek] one who is averse to censuring others for minor matters, who has a pleasant countenance,
has conquered the senses, is well-contented, wise, and observes celibacy.
Having abandoned the instability of mental and physical ailments, and being free from the distress of evil suspicions,
one is eager for the service, devotion, and attendance upon the discourse, praise, and meditation of the Guru.
O Goddess, [one who is] devoted to the guru and the deity, eager for the worship of the Kāminī,
an observer of the guru’s commands, and a praiser of the guru’s fame.
O Mistress of the Clan, [one should choose a disciple] who knows the authority of the Guru’s words, who delights in service to the Guru,
who follows his mind, and who acts with circumspection.
Free from shame, pride, arrogance, and the like, remaining indifferent toward the teacher's property in the presence of the guru, and longing for his grace.
The Guru should accept as a disciple one who is devoted to the meditations on form and so forth, who proceeds toward the path of liberation, and who is endowed with such characteristics as these.
The characteristics of a bad disciple: one born of a wicked lineage, wicked, devoid of virtues, deformed,
a former disciple of another, a heretic, a rogue, and one who fancies himself a scholar.

One whose limbs are deficient, excessive, or deformed, who possesses impaired members, who is lame, blind, deaf, filthy, or afflicted by disease; one who is impure, foul-mouthed, or a libertine wearing whatever attire he pleases.
He is poorly educated, ill-behaved, crooked, and has a terrifying gaze;
he is possessed by sleep and laziness, and is addicted to lethargy, gambling, and other such vices.
One whose body is always hidden behind doors, walls, pillars, and the like;
who is devoid of emptiness and liberation; who is base and destitute of faith and devotion.
Who is that single speaker— arrogant, a detractor, fickle,
and deceitful— who is devoid of wealth, wife, and purity, and who is abandoned by both prohibitions and injunctions?
One who reveals secrets, one who thwarts the purposes of the gods,
one who behaves like a cat or a crow, and one who is intent on seeking out faults.
14) One who is full of deceit, ungrateful, one who gives secretly while hiding [the gift] within,
a betrayer of trust, a hater of the gods, and a doer of evil.

One who is untrustworthy, one whose limb is ignorance, one who desires the accomplishment of misfortune, an assailant, one who seeks to seize [another's property], one who is contemptible, and a false witness— [these should not be questioned].
O Goddess, [one should avoid] a beggar everywhere, one who goes to all places of attraction,
one whose ultimate aim is untruth, one who is unattached [to virtue], and one who speaks excessively about vulgar matters and the like.
One who causes ill-considered thoughts and fallacious reasoning, who is fond of quarreling,
who makes groundless accusations, who is deluded, who leads others astray, and who mocks with words.
One who finds fault behind one's back but speaks kindly in one's presence,
and who utters harsh words while praising himself— know such a person to be a thief of speech.
Intolerant of virtues, fearful of the righteous, filled with excessive anger,
a Cārvāka who is a friend to the wicked and despised by all the world.
One who is slanderous, who torments others, who causes fear to all living beings, who speaks words that cause distress, who betrays friends, and who deceives his own brothers.
O Goddess, one who is devoted to the tongue and the genitals, who acts like a thief and a beast,
and who indulges in causeless hatred, laughter, affliction, anger, and the like— [is such a person].
One who commits excessive ridicule, who mocks others from within a state of delusion,
who is lustful and utterly shameless, and who indicates false and wicked conduct— [these are the faults].
Endowed with envy, intoxication, and avarice, joined with hypocrisy and egoism,
[he is] characterized by jealousy, calumny, harshness, miserliness, anger, and pride.
One who is impatient, suffering, hateful, incapable, devoid of truth,
lacking renown, foolish, and whose mind is agitated by anxiety.
O Dear One, he is possessed by thirst and greed, wretched, discontented, a priest for all, a glutton, deceitful, a deceiver, and crooked.
Devoid of devotion, faith, compassion, tranquility, and righteous conduct,
it causes laughter among mothers, fathers, gurus, the wise, and the great.

O Mistress of the Kula, [one who is] loathsome regarding family property and the like, who is conceited about serving the Guru, who is corrupt with women, who has fallen from the observances, and who is cursed by the Guru.
A teacher should abandon a disciple who is possessed of such defects as these;
yet, if out of affection or for the sake of appearance he accepts him, he should initiate him.
15) A divine curse shall fall upon that guru together with his disciple.
Therefore, one should by no means accept such a disciple;
if he accepts him out of delusion, the guru is tainted by those very sins.
Just as the sin committed by a wife touches her husband,
so too does the sin committed by a disciple generally touch the teacher as well.
The teacher should examine the disciple through both knowledge and conduct for one year, or half of that, or half of that again, or even half of that;
[he should test] those of superior [capacity] in inferior tasks and those of inferior [capacity] in superior tasks.
By means of gifts of life or wealth, through commands both fair and foul, by words that pierce their vital spots, by deceptions, and by cruel deeds;
With partialities, with indifference, and with many [other states], again and again.
Even when reviled or afflicted, he who does not fall into despondency should always reflect with joy: "The Guru is showing compassion."
Whether in the remembrance of the glorious Guru, or in his glorification, or in salutation, in service, in invocation, in sending forth, or in seeking him— O beloved—
one experiences transformations such as bliss, trembling, horripilation, and changes in voice and eyes.
O Goddess, those who possess these qualities shall be fit for this, and may even attain the perfection of mantras;
having ascertained their capacity for awakening, one should become a disciple, and not otherwise.

O Goddess, disciples are proclaimed to be inferior, middling, or superior according as they are fit for the beginning, the middle, or the end [of practice], and according as they are struck by [the descent of] power (śakti).
O Goddess, those who say that devotion must first exist for the sake of initiation,
yet whose disposition is subsequently lost, are said to be "fit for the beginning" (ādiyogya).
Those who have received initiation and the observance of the rules, yet are devoid of knowledge and realization,
and whose potency has consequently been destroyed, are remembered as being "intermediate" (madhyayogya).
Those who are devoid of devotion at the beginning, yet possess it— or lack it— during the middle,
but come to have abundant devotion at the end, they become fit for the final goal.
In the *Nārāyaṇīya*: "One who performs service to the teacher through the actions of mind, speech, and body;
who is pure in disposition and possesses great enthusiasm—such a person is known as a disciple."
The son is to be instructed, as are the *vyatyayin* and the *vasuda*.
The *vyatyayin* is one who, having given one mantra, receives another mantra. And it is said elsewhere:
"Knowledge [is obtained] through service to the guru, or by means of abundant wealth."
"Or rather, knowledge does not arise from knowledge; thus the fourth [initiation] is not applicable.

In the *Prapañcasāra*: "He who is constantly desirous of service with body, speech, and mind for a period of three, two, or one year, and whose mind is well-restrained, should be accepted as a disciple."
In the *Mantramuktāvalī*: "Between those two, within the span of a single year, there will arise mutual knowledge;
whether one holds the status of guru or disciple, it shall not be otherwise—this is the certain conclusion.
And the disciple, having received the mantra from the true guru, should eventually relinquish it."
A disciple who abandons the guru will certainly be subject to penance.
Thus, according to the statement of the *Liṅgāgama*, even the abandonment of a mantra obtained from an unworthy teacher (*asadguru*) is the intended meaning of the scripture.
As it is said in another tantra: "If by chance a man of the Kula lineage obtains the Vidyā from a bound soul (*paśu*), he should, upon reaching a Kaulika twice-born, receive the Vidyā once again."
In the Devyāgama: "For one who undergoes the initiation of a bound soul (paśu), there will certainly be suffering of the limbs as a consequence;
of this there is no doubt, or else there will be imprisonment."
Having written that mantra on a banyan leaf, one should cast it into a stream;
or, having taken refuge in a true guru, one should receive the consecrated mantra.
In the Kulārṇava: "O Goddess, having obtained a venerable Guru who possesses the [required] characteristics, who severs all doubt, and who bestows knowledge, one should not resort to another Guru."
Having approached a teacher who is ignorant and unable to sever one's doubts,
a disciple who goes to another teacher is not defiled by the faults of the former.
In the Śaiva Āgama as well: "There are many gurus who know evil spells and medicinal herbs;
one who knows the mantras taught in the Vedas and Āgamas is rare on earth."
A wise person may rescue a fool, but a fool cannot rescue a fool;
for can a boat carry across a stone? Indeed, could a stone carry across a stone?
Just as a bee, greedy for honey, goes from flower to another flower,
so too a disciple, greedy for knowledge, goes from teacher to another teacher.
Thus, when there is mutual contradiction among the statements of the tantras, one must accept only that method taught by one's own guru.
As it is said in that very same work:
"Many paths have been proclaimed by the wise in the science of mantra."
Relying on the opinion of one's own guru, one should perform what is auspicious, and not otherwise.
Thus ends the characteristics of the disciple (17). Now follows the procedure for initiation (*dīkṣāvidhi*) according to the *Mahākapilapañcarātra*:
"There is no entitlement for Śūdras to the mantras; there is a supreme restriction [against them].
Because of the absence of mantras, every ritual act is indeed performed without mantras. Thus it is stated in the *Śātātapa-saṃhitā*.
"Prajāpati himself has declared that for as many syllables as one might cause a mantra to be imparted to a woman or a Śūdra, there would be that many instances of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa."
In the Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa: "The mantras should indeed be given to those Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras who are pure and stainless, but not to those of mixed caste."
In the Devīyāmala: "If a twice-born man gives a mantra joined with the *svāhā* and the *praṇava* to a Śūdra, the Śūdra shall go to hell and the Brāhmaṇa shall attain the state of a Śūdra."
In the *Brahma Purāṇa*: "The Vedic or the mixed [path] is prescribed for the Brahmins and others;
the Tantric [path] is proclaimed even for a Śūdra who is devoted to a Brahmin."
Women and Śūdras should also perform the worship of Viṣṇu with faith according to the path taught in their own scriptures, having placed their husband in their hearts.
Women also have the right to perform the worship of Viṣṇu and other such rites, provided they are devoted to pleasing their husbands; this is the eternal Vedic revelation.
In the Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa: "A woman who is separated from her husband, yet auspicious and endowed with virtuous conduct, should receive the mantras together with her husband, by his permission."
Whatever act of propitiating deities or the like is performed apart from one’s own duty (svadharma) will crumble in an instant, like a palace built of sand.
In the Kulārṇava: "For a widow, by the command of her son; for a maiden, by the order of her father;
for women and Śūdras, this mantra ending in 'namas' brings happiness."
Having understood this, O Great Goddess, one may initiate even Cāṇḍālas;
however, a Śūdra or a woman should never recite Vedic mantras.
The wise desire either a Śaiva mantra or a Vaiṣṇava mantra that ends with "namas."

Thus [it is said]. From the *Yājñavalkya-saṃhitā* (in the *Śāradā*): "A Brāhmaṇa becomes fit [for initiation] after one year from the Guru, a Kṣatriya after two years, a Vaiśya after three years, and a Śūdra after four years."
18) He is one who desires to hear and is to be accepted for the initiatory consecration, sacrifices, vows, and so forth.

In the *Tantrarāja*: "Having observed the suitability over one, two, three, four, or five years, [the teacher should accept] those endowed with devotion and virtues, according to the sequence of castes and mixed castes."
In the Kulārṇava: "A Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, or indeed a Śūdra may become a Manu;
it should be given in the direct order (anuloma), never in the inverse order (pratiloma)."
In the Vāmakeśvara [Tantra], however, five divisions are stated: "Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and those of eastern origin. In the Sautrāmaṇi Tantra:
"The seed-syllable *māyā* (hīṃ) is the Brāhmaṇa; the seed-syllable *śrī* (śrīṃ) is remembered as the Kṣatriya."
The seed-syllable of desire (Kāma) is for the Vaiśya, while Vāgbhava is said to be for the Śūdra.
A mantra devoid of four seed-syllables is designated as "eastern.
For Brāhmaṇas, it should have four seed-syllables; for Kṣatriyas, three seed-syllables.
The Vaiśyas have two seed-syllables (bījas), while the Śūdras have only one.
In the *Kulamūlāvatāra*, the Goddess said:
"Regarding the Śākta, Śāmbhava, Saura, Gāṇeśa, and Vaiṣṇava [traditions]..."
Especially for the castes such as Brahmins and Kṣatriyas, and for those born of mixed unions.
I wish to hear about the ritual application for the benefit of practitioners;
O Śaṅkara, tell me the divisions of those mantras according to which [practitioners] they belong.
Īśvara said: Umā, Maheśvara, Dakṣiṇāmūrtti, Aghora, Hayagrīva, Vārāha, and thereafter the eight-syllabled mantra (Aṣṭākṣara).
Vāsudeva preceded by the *praṇava* (oṃ), as well as Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa,
should be given to those of the three [twice-born] castes, but never to any other caste.
The Pāśupata, the Nārasiṃha, and likewise the Sudarśana [mantras] should be given to those of two castes, and never to anyone else.
Whatever mantras of Agni there may be, as well as those of Sūrya,
and the mantras beginning with Tārā and ending with Ghṛṇi, should be bestowed upon the Trivarṇaka.
The *anuṣṭubh* meter, the *śakti-mantras*,
as well as Vindhyavāsinī and Nīlasarasvatī, should be assigned to the first letter.
Mātaṅginī, Ugratārā, Kālikā, Śyāmalā,
as well as Chinnamastā and Bālā, should be assigned to every color.
19) Tārādi, Gaṇeśa, and likewise the one named Haridrā should be given specifically to women among those of the three castes.
The Praṇava, Māyā, Lakṣmī, Vāgbhava, and another seed-syllable—
joined with these seeds, it should be bestowed upon the first letter.
The *māyā* (hrīṃ), *lakṣmī* (śrīṃ), and *vāgbhava* (aiṃ) should be given even to Kṣatriyas;
and *lakṣmī* and *vāgbhava* are likewise prescribed for the Vaiśya caste.

The Vāgbhava seed-syllable and other seed-syllables are prescribed for Śūdras; for those of mixed caste (saṃkara), the use of the heart-mantra (hṛdaya) and so forth, beginning with *hūṃ* and *phaṭ*, is recommended.
In the *Bhūtaḍāmara*: "Now we shall declare those mantras which bestow success in the Kali age:
the three-syllabled Nṛsiṃha, the Kūṭa, and the Anuṣṭubh Nṛkeśarī."
Hayagrīva, as well as Kūṭa, Anuṣṭub Hayānana,
Kūṭa Cintāmaṇi, Kūṭa Kṣetrapāla, and Bhairava.
Trijatā, Ekajatā, Kālī, Nīlasarasvatī, Śavarī,
Tripurā, Rāmā, Brahmatārā, and Piśācinī.
Mātaṅgī, Dhanadā, Śyāmā, Mahogrā, Kālasundarī,
Ugratārā, the King of Yakṣas, the Yakṣiṇīs, and likewise the handmaidens.

In the Kali age, these Manus are declared to be equal to wish-fulfilling trees (kalpadrumas), bestowing both visible and invisible fruits; they have been proclaimed in all the Tantras and kept secret.
Now, regarding the time for initiation (*dīkṣā*):
first, the months. In the *Śrīkaṇṭhasaṃhitā*:
"Initiation during the autumn season and in Vaiśākha bestows the most excellent fruit."
It is most excellent in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa and Phālguna, but in Jyeṣṭha it is indeed inferior.
In the month of Māgha it bestows auspiciousness, but in the month of Āṣāḍha it is wicked;
in the month of Śrāvaṇa it is joyful, while in the months of Pauṣa and Bhādrapada it is censured.
In the *Āgamakalpadruma*: "Initiation in Caitra leads to suffering; in Vaiśākha, there is an accumulation of jewels;
in Jyeṣṭha, death occurs; and in Āṣāḍha, there is the loss of kinsmen."
In Śrāvaṇa there will surely be prosperity, while in Bhādrapada there will be decline;
in Āśvina, however, there will be the destruction of the people and indeed only inauspiciousness.
In Kārttika there shall be knowledge, and in Mārgaśīrṣa there will indeed be happiness;
in Pauṣa there is the loss of knowledge, while in Māgha there is the increase of intelligence.
20) In Phālguna, there shall be complete success; one should avoid an intercalary month (mala-māsa). Āṣāḍha is sometimes stated to be suitable as well. As it is said:
"The commencement of mantra practice in the month preceding Vaiśākha is very difficult to endure."
In Vaiśākha it bestows wealth, but in Jyaiṣṭha it becomes a giver of death.
In Āṣāḍha, it is for the attainment of a son; in Śrāvaṇa, it is considered to bestow auspiciousness;
and in Bhādrapada, the loss of knowledge is proclaimed by the wise.
In Āśvina there is complete success; in Kārttika it bestows the attainment of knowledge;
Mārgaśīrṣa shall be auspicious; and in Pauṣa it brings about suffering.

"In Māgha there is an increase of intelligence, and in Phālguna there is subjugation of all. Thus it is said. In the *Siddhāntaśekhara*: "Initiation during the autumn season and in Vaiśākha bestows the most excellent fruit;
initiation in Phālguna, Mārgaśīrṣa, and Jyeṣṭha is middling."
The months of Āṣāḍha, Śrāvaṇa, and Māgha are declared by the wise to be the least auspicious;
likewise, the months of Caitra, Pauṣa, and Bhādrapada are censured.
Even during months that are censured, initiation is declared to be auspicious during an eclipse;
as stated in the *Gautamīya-tantra*: "The commencement of mantra practice in the month of Caitra bestows all human goals."
In Vaiśākha there shall be the acquisition of jewels; in Jyeṣṭha, however, death is certain.
In Āṣāḍha there shall be the loss of kinsmen, while in Śrāvaṇa one shall attain a full lifespan.
In Bhādrapada there will be the destruction of progeny; in Āśvina, a collection of jewels;
in Kārttika, there will be the accomplishment of mantras; and it shall be the same in Mārgaśīrṣa.
In Pauṣa, there will be affliction from enemies; in Māgha, there is an increase in intelligence;
in Phālguna, all desires shall be fulfilled; one should avoid the intercalary month (mala-māsa).
In this context, the injunction regarding Caitra refers to the initiation (*dīkṣā*) for the Gopāla mantra. As stated in the *Kālottara*:
"The conjunction of autumn and spring is prescribed for the performance of the rite of initiation;
in their absence, it is commended at other times, except during the rainy season."
In the *Kriyākāṇḍaśekhara*:
"Initiation cannot take place except on a festival day (*parvan*), during the rainy season, or in the months of Caitra and Pauṣa.
In the *Kāraṇa*: "And in the month preceding Āṣāḍha, as well as in Āṣāḍha and Mārgaśīrṣa."

"A wise man should not perform the initiation in another month; rather, he should perform it [in the prescribed month]. Thus concludes the determination of the months. 21) Now follows the determination of the fortnights (pakṣa).
In the *Agastyasaṃhitā*:
"Whether in the bright fortnight or the dark fortnight, initiation brings all auspiciousness.
But in the *Kālottara*: "Those desiring liberation [should perform it] in the dark fortnight; those desiring prosperity, always in the bright [fortnight]."
Thus it has been stated. In the *Gautamīya-tantra*:

"Initiation is auspicious during the bright fortnight (*śukla-pakṣa*), and also during the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇa*) up until the fifth day. In another tantra: "In the bright fortnight there shall be the attainment of desired goals; in the dark fortnight, however, it bestows inauspiciousness."
Likewise: "The dark fortnight becomes bright until the day of the eighth of the dark fortnight.
Now, the determination of the lunar days (*tithi*) according to the Tantra: "On the first, the second, and the third [lunar days], one should remain pure."
On the fourth day there will be loss of wealth; on the fifth day there is an increase of intelligence.
On the sixth day, there is the destruction of knowledge; on the seventh day, one obtains happiness;
on the eighth day, there will be the loss of intellect; and on the ninth day, the decay of the body.
On the tenth day there is royal fortune; on the eleventh, one becomes pure;
on the twelfth, all success shall be attained; and on the thirteenth, there is poverty.

On the fourteenth day, there is birth as an animal; at the end of the month, there is loss. On the full moon day of the fortnight sacred to Viṣṇu, there shall be an increase in merit; one should avoid Vedic study during these times, as well as when there is thundering at twilight, an earthquake, or the falling of meteors.
One should avoid these and other days even as prescribed by the Śruti.
In the *Sārasaṃgraha*: "The full moon, the fifth, the second, the seventh, the thirteenth, and the tenth are auspicious for all ritual acts."
In the Vijayamālinītantra:
"The fifth, the eleventh, the seventh, the thirteenth,
the tenth, and especially the twelfth of the bright fortnight [are auspicious]."
In the *Mantrasārasaṃgraha*: "It should be performed especially on the third, the fifth, or the sixth lunar day; it may also be performed on the twelfth or even on the thirteenth."
In the Rudrayāmala: "The rite of initiation on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight bestows auspiciousness.
In the Ratnāvalī: "Excluding the fourth, ninth, sixth, eighth, fourteenth, and full moon days, the remaining lunar days are said to be beneficial for those seeking liberation."
22) In the *Tattvasārasaṃhitā*:
"Having carefully considered each respective lunar day (*tithi*), one should initiate those who are devoted to that [deity] on that day.
Likewise: "The full moon (*paurṇamāsī*) is prescribed for Brahmā, and the twelfth day (*dvādaśī*) for the Wielder of the Discus (Viṣṇu)."
The fourteenth day is said to belong to Śiva, while the thirteenth is said to belong to Vāc.
The second is said to belong to Śrī, the third to Pārvatī,
the fourth to Gaṇanātha, and the seventh is said to belong to Bhānu.
Regarding the regular paths for Pārvatī, the eighth and fourteenth lunar days are prescribed.
In the *Nāradapañcarātra*: "On the twelfth day of the bright fortnight, as well as during the sun's transit (*saṃkramaṇa*).
In the *Gautamīyatantra*: "It should be performed on the twelfth day by all means, and on the auspicious day of the *Amalā*."
That Dvādaśī is dear to Kṛṣṇa; it is the initiator of initiation into Kṛṣṇa.
In the *Kālottara*: "Excluding the intercalary days of the month, those [days] which touch upon three lunar days [are significant].
In another Tantra: "The new moon on a Monday, the fourteenth day on a Tuesday, and the seventh day on a Sunday are equal to hundreds of solar festivals (*sūryaparvan*)."
Now, the determination of the days [for initiation] is stated in the *Gautamīya-tantra*: "It should be performed on Sunday, Thursday, Saturday, Monday, Mercury, or Friday.
Regarding "Monday," it is recommended during the bright fortnight (*śukla-pakṣa*), whereas it is prohibited during the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇa-pakṣa*). Thus it has been said:
Regarding the true nature of mantras: the commencement of a mantra should take place on Sunday, Wednesday, or especially on Thursday;
on Saturday there is death, on Tuesday there is loss, and on Monday everything is fruitless.

In the *Ratnāvalī*: "For the sake of prosperity, one should avoid the days of Āditya (Sunday), Maṅgala (Tuesday), and Sauri (Saturday). Now follows the determination of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).
In the *Gautamīya-tantra*: "The three *uttarās*, Rohiṇī, Revatī, Puṣya, and Vāsava (Jyeṣṭhā)..."
Dhaniṣṭhā, Vāyu, Mitra, Agni, Pitrya, Tvāṣṭra, and Nairṛta.
The hands of Īśa (Īśāna) and Viṣṇu are auspicious for initiation (*dīkṣā*).
Jyeṣṭhā belongs to Vāsava; Svāti to Vāyu; Anurādhā to Mitra; Maghā to Pitrya; Citrā to Tvaṣṭṛ; Mūla to Nairṛta; Ārdrā to Īśa; and Śravaṇa to Vaiṣṇava.
In the Agastyasaṃhitā: "One should perform the mantra-consecration under the asterisms of Aśvinī, Rohiṇī, Svātī, Viśākhā, Hasta, and likewise under Jyeṣṭhā and the three Uttarās."
In the *Ratnāvalī*: "The three Uttarās, Rohiṇī, Puṣya, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Hasta, Svāti, Anurādhā, Maghā, Mūla, and Revatī."
23) And "hearing from the light" (ābhājacchravaṇaṃ) is the most excellent initiation asterism.
In the *Kāraṇa*: "Pauṣṇa, Rohiṇī, then Āditya, Śravaṇa, and likewise Aśvinī;
Sāvitra, Tvāṣṭra, Vāyavya, Aindra, and also Nairṛta."
O you of virtuous vows, the constellations Tiṣya (Puṣya), the three Uttarās, Ārdrā, Saumya (Mṛgaśiras), and the birth-star of the disciple are praised for the rite of initiation.
Revatī belongs to Pūṣan; Punarvasu belongs to Āditya; Hastā belongs to Savitṛ; Mṛgaśiras belongs to Soma.
In the Nīlatantra it is said: "Rohiṇī, Śravaṇa, Ārdrā, Dhaniṣṭhā, the three Uttarās, Puṣya, and Śatabhiṣaj are declared to be the lunar mansions for initiation (dīkṣā)."
In the Tantra— specifically in the third, the seventh, as well as the sixteenth, the eighteenth, the nineteenth,
the twenty-first, and likewise the twenty-third.

One should avoid performing auspicious rites under the twenty-five lunar mansions. In the Śaiva Āgama it is said: "Under a downward-facing auspicious mansion, and especially when there is purity of the moon, one should employ the strength of the stars during the dark fortnight, while contemplating the initial letters of one's own name."
In the *Ratnāvalī*: "The first lunar day with the constellation Pūrvāṣāḍhā, likewise the fifth with Kṛttikā;
the sixth with Pūrvabhādrapadā, and likewise the tenth with Rohiṇī."
The twelfth lunar day when conjoined with the asterism Āśleṣā, and the thirteenth when conjoined with the asterism Puṣya—
these are known as "asterism-deprived" (nakṣatraluptā), and they bring destruction even to the gods.
Now, the determination of the yogas is stated in the *Ratnāvalī*: "Yoga, Prīti, Āyuṣmān, Saubhāgya, Śobhana, Śubha,
Sukarman, Dhṛti, Buddhi, Dhruva, Siddhi, and Harṣaṇa."
Varīyān, Śiva, Siddha, Brahmā, and Indra are the sixteen [deities].
In the *Gautamīya-tantra*: "In all auspicious conjunctions (*yoga*), initiation (*dīkṣā*) bestows all that is auspicious.
Now follows the determination of the instruments (*karaṇa*).
In the Gautamīya Tantra: "They say that auspicious instruments [of action] are required, especially for initiation;
one should specifically avoid the *viṣṭi* yoga and [inauspicious] periods such as *śakuni*."
Now, the determination of the ascendant (lagna) according to the *Sārasaṃgraha*: "The commencement of mantras and other rites in Aries shall bestow wealth and grain;
in Taurus, one meets with death; in Gemini, there is the loss of offspring."
24) In Cancer there shall be all success; in Leo, the destruction of intelligence;
Virgo constantly bestows fortune; and in Libra, all accomplishments.
In Scorpio there shall be all success; Sagittarius is the destroyer of knowledge;
Capricorn is said to bestow sons; and Aquarius grants the abundance of wealth.

Pisces always bestows suffering; such, O beloved, is the fruit of the zodiac signs. In the Śaiva Āgama: "The morning hour bestows dharma, the *saṅgava* [mid-morning] grants sovereignty, at midday there shall be all success, and the afternoon would be mediocre."
However, the night is forbidden for the imparting of mantras by the best of teachers.

In the Gautamīya Tantra: A movable sign (cara-rāśi) should be avoided by all [for initiation], whereas a fixed sign (sthira-rāśi) bestows happiness. A fixed ascendant (lagna) is auspicious for the Viṣṇu mantra, while a movable one is auspicious for the Śiva mantra.
A lagna situated in the second or twelfth house is praised for the Śakti-mantra;
malefic planets should occupy the third, sixth, and eleventh houses, while benefic planets should be placed in the angles (kendras) and the trines (trikoṇas).
In the case of initiation (*dīkṣā*), all [planets] situated in the eighth house (*randhra*) are auspicious, yet they cause the destruction of everything.
In the *Tantra*, the Moon situated in the third, eleventh, sixth, or tenth house is auspicious;
the Moon at birth is declared auspicious provided it is devoid of its natal asterism (*janmanakṣatra*).
In the bright fortnight, the second, fifth, and ninth lunar days are auspicious;
even if joined with planets that are pure in their course, the Moon is favorable.
Or even when situated in a neutral [sign], the Moon shall bestow auspicious results.
In the Gautamīya Tantra: "On a day pure in its five limbs, at the rising of the Moon or the Sun, and indeed during the rising of Jupiter and Venus, the excellent performance of mantra is commended."

In the Vārāhītantra: "If Venus is set or has reached its period of decline, or if Jupiter and the Sun are [in conjunction], then initiation is not to be performed when [the Moon] is in Aries, Scorpio, or Leo."

Likewise: on the birth-star of the disciple, during a transit (saṃkrānti), at the equinoxes (viṣuva) and solstices (ayana), on other auspicious conjunctions (puṇyayoga), and during lunar or solar eclipses.
On the five parvan days, on the first day of a yuga, and on days such as the vyatīpāta yoga, initiation is declared to be auspicious; no further deliberation is required in this matter.

In the Yoginītantra: "Indeed, that purification of the month, lunar day, weekday, and so forth which has been taught, should be understood by the best of practitioners as being primarily for the purpose of mantra-initiation."
For the initiation into knowledge (vidyādīkṣā), there is no purification of lunar days, weekdays, and so forth;
rather, the initiation occurs whenever there is a desire, in accordance with the command of the Guru.
25) Now, regarding the refutation [of restrictions], it is said in the *Kriyākāṇḍaśekhara*: "Furthermore, for one seeking liberation (*maumukṣu*), no restriction of time and so forth is prescribed;
all those [restrictions] are censured, whereas [these practices] are praised for the sake of liberation."

In the Tantra: "During an eclipse of the moon or sun, at the birth of the disciple, at the transit of the sun into Capricorn, and at the time of the Guru’s [display of] compassion—no [specific] lunar mansion or other such factors is required for initiation."

In the Rudrayāmala: "At a sacred pilgrimage site, during an eclipse of the sun or moon, or on the Damanaka festival, one who undergoes mantra-initiation need not purify the month, the lunar mansion, and so forth."
In the Yoginītantra: "During the transit of the sun and likewise during a solar eclipse, one should never at any time consider such things as the ascendant (lagna) and so forth."
Especially on the Mahāṣṭamī, for the sake of attaining wealth and desired goals,
it is stated in the Agastyasaṃhitā: "At the time of a solar eclipse, nothing else need be sought."
There is nothing whatsoever equal to the time of a solar eclipse.
In that regard, whatever is performed there shall all yield infinite fruit;
on the occasion of a solar eclipse, there is no need for the purification of the month, lunar day, weekday, and so forth.
Whatever desired [gift] is accepted from a guru among men at that time,
then the mantra indeed becomes effective without effort.
It should be performed with every effort by those desiring the accomplishment (*siddhi*) of mantra.
In the *Śaktiyāmala*: "A lunar eclipse is equal to a thousand solar eclipses;
therefore, an eclipse on one's own [natal] day is said to be a hundred-thousandfold more efficacious."
However, in another tantra it is said: "In that regard, a solar eclipse is recommended, but a lunar eclipse is never [recommended].
In the Viṣṇuyāmala: "Beginning from the awakening of the Goddess (Devī) until the ninth lunar day (navamī), initiation performed by the wise during those [days] bestows all desired fruits."
Likewise: "In the case of the awakening of Durgā, one should not examine whether the time is auspicious or inauspicious;
it is when there is the eighth day called Aśoka and likewise the ninth day called Rāmā."
In the *Samayātantra*: "On the first day of the Yuga, on one's birthday, likewise on the day of marriage, and during the two solstices and equinoxes—one should not deliberate upon anything at all."

Elsewhere it is also said: "During the solstices, the equinoxes, likewise on the anniversaries of the Yugas, during eclipses, and at great sacred sites (tīrthas), there is no need for consideration of the time."
Near a *tulasī* plant, at the root of a *vilva* tree, likewise at the foot of a *dhātrī* tree,
in the presence of the Anādi-deva, in a great sacred field (*mahākṣetra*), or in a cowshed.

On the day of the worship of the Goddess (Devīpūjā), there is no fixed determination regarding the time. As stated in the Yoginītantra: "The initiation received during a lunar eclipse, the initiation of forest-dwellers, and the initiation of one's father—these result in poverty for seven births."

In the Rudrayāmala, however, it is said: "One should not perform a Śākta initiation when the sun is eclipsed, nor should one perform a Vaiṣṇava initiation during an eclipse of the moon. And in the Muṇḍamālā: "Kālī, Tārā, Mahāvidyā, Ṣoḍaśī, and Bhuvaneśvarī..."
Bhairavī, Chinnamastā, and likewise the Vidyā Dhūmāvatī.
Bagalā, Siddhavidyā, Mātaṅgī, and Kamalātmikā—
these alone, O Maheśānī, are proclaimed as the Mahāvidyās.
In this [practice], there is no dependence on perfected beings (siddhas) and the like, nor any consideration of constellations and so forth;
there is no purification of time and the like, nor indeed any defect regarding the object to be accomplished (sādhya).
In the *Tattvasāgarasaṃhitā*:
"Listen to the special occasion for initiation even without regard for the lunar day (*tithi*):
when the rare opportunity of meeting a true Guru occurs but once."
When permission for that is obtained, that is the great occasion for initiation—
whether in a village or in a forest, in a sacred field or by day or by night.
When the Guru arrives by chance, then initiation should take place;
likewise, initiation occurs whenever there is a desire, in accordance with the command of the Guru.
There is no lunar day, no vow, no fire-oblation, no ritual bathing, and no recitation of mantras—no such ritual action is required.
What, then, is the cause for initiation? When a true Guru has been obtained according to one's own wish, there is a specific rule regarding the Tārā mantra in the *Mahogratārākalpa*:
on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, at an auspicious moment and under a favorable planetary configuration.
In the bright fortnight of Pūrvabhādrapadā, well-conjoined with the constellation Maitra (Anurādhā).
Alternatively, it is highly commended under Anurādhā or Revatī;
one should recognize this as an auspicious time for the reception of the mantra.
Especially during the month of Āśvina and particularly during Kārttika,
there is no fault in wearing blue garments according to the Mahācīna method.
In the *Vīracūḍāmaṇi*: "There is no enemy of the Siddhas, nor Tārā, nor the purification of the zodiacal circle;
there is neither debt nor wealth, nor the [astrological] wheel, nor likewise any restriction regarding months."
27) One should not avoid the lunar fortnight, the lunar day, or the asterism; nor should one avoid Tuesdays and Saturdays.
Thus concludes the determination of time.
Now, the place.

In the *Yāmala*: "At a holy pilgrimage site (*puṇyatīrtha*), at Kurukṣetra, at the four seats of the Goddess (*devīpīṭha*), at Prayāga, on Śrīgiri, and at Kāśī, one need not distinguish between the proper and improper time."
In the Yoginītantra: "At Gayā, in the field of Bhāskara, at Virajā, on Mount Candra, at Catvara, at Mataṅga, and likewise in the hermitages of Kanyā."
Therefore, O Pārvatī, one should not receive initiation at these sacred sites (tīrthas).
Now, regarding the greatness of initiation, the Vārāhītantra states: "The death of one who is uninitiated does not lead to liberation from Raurava."
Therefore, those who follow the Tantras should perform initiation by relying upon the Tantra.
In the Mṛḍānītantra: "He who is deluded by māyā and enveloped by sins may despise initiation; indeed, he shall become a denizen of hell."
Elsewhere it is also said: "Action performed by one devoid of initiation is like an oblation poured into ashes;
for a mortal who lacks the Lord, there is no protector on earth."
Likewise, for one devoid of initiation, there is no master either in this world or in the next.
In the *Mahāhāraka-tantra*: "Now, he who exists on earth devoid of initiation, suffering the fruits of his sins, falls miserable into the pit of hell in the darkness of delusion."
One who is devoid of initiation is perpetually impure and unfit for all ritual acts;
whatever else he performs out of delusion, he shall not partake of its fruit.
In the Rudrayāmala: "O lady of beautiful thighs, everything performed by one who is uninitiated is useless;
a man devoid of initiation and impure attains birth in the womb of a beast."

In the Vārāhī Tantra: "The entire world has initiation as its root; initiation is indeed the supreme austerity. A man may dwell in whatever stage of life (āśrama) he chooses, provided he relies upon initiation."
Whatever sin has been committed throughout ten million births, whether done knowingly or unknowingly—
one is liberated from all such sins merely by receiving initiation.
From that, there shall be the accomplishment of one's desires, bestowing an abundance of wealth and grain;
in the end, endowed with divine enjoyments, one goes to the abode of the gods.
In the Mahāhāraka Tantra: "Knowledge is bestowed and the accumulation of sins is utterly destroyed;
therefore it is called initiation (dīkṣā), which accomplishes one's desired aims."
28) Since it bestows divine knowledge and effects the destruction of the sins of men,
it is therefore proclaimed as *dīkṣā* in this world by those who have mastered the Tantras.

By taking refuge in initiation, a person destroys the sins of killing a Brahmin, drinking liquor, stealing gold, and other such major offenses, as well as hundreds of thousands of minor transgressions.
An initiated Brāhmaṇa goes to the stainless world of Brahmā;
likewise, a Kṣatriya goes to the world of Indra, and a Vaiśya to that of Prajāpati.
A Śūdra goes to the city of the Gandharvas through the power of initiation;
therefore, initiation is praised for all four castes alone.
In the Vaiśampāyana-saṃhitā:
"Whatever sin has been accumulated through mind, action, or speech,
[this practice] causes their dissolution, since it bestows supreme knowledge."
Therefore, it is proclaimed in this world by those who know the scriptures that this is called *dīkṣā*.
In another Tantra it is said: "O beautiful one, for him by whom a mantra written in a book is recited, no accomplishment arises; there is only loss at every step."

In the *Tantrarāja*: "A mantra that has not been received from a preceptor, or one that has been received but for which the ritual fee (*dakṣiṇā*) has not been given—even if recited constantly—does not attain accomplishment."
Just as twice-born men who lack the sacred thread have no entitlement here to their own duties, such as Vedic study, nor to rites such as the initiation ceremony (upanayana).
Likewise, those who have not received initiation have no authority regarding the worship of mantras and deities; therefore, one should make oneself consecrated by Śiva.
In another tantra it is said: "Whether heard by chance, or even in secret or through deception, or seen on paper like a mere verse, even if it has been recited, it is fruitless."
In the *Prayogasāra*: "If one who is uninitiated accepts [the transmission] out of affection or even greed, then a curse from the deity shall fall upon that guru together with his disciples."
Elsewhere also it is said: "All rites, when performed with the Guru as the primary agent, bestow the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
therefore, one should always strive for a Guru who is exceedingly composed."
Since all ritual acts performed without the instruction of a guru will certainly be fruitless, the path prescribed in the Śrutis was for the Kṛta age, that arising from the Smṛtis for the Tretā,
that spoken in the Purāṇas for the Dvāpara, and that originating from the Āgamas for the Kali age.
For those Brahmins born in the Kali age who are impure and akin to Śūdras,
spiritual accomplishment (siddhi) may occur through the path of traditional scripture (āgama), but not by way of the Vedic path (śrauta).
Therefore, initiation (*dīkṣā*) is essential according to the many previously mentioned scriptural statements;
having investigated it thoroughly, it should be received according to the various divisions such as the zodiacal signs (*rāśi*) and the like.
In the *Kulārṇava*: "Those who perform rites such as recitation (*japa*) and fire-offerings (*homa*) without being initiated..."
O beloved, their [good deeds] do not bear fruit, like seeds sown upon a stone.

Now, regarding the examination of the ground for the purpose of the pavilion used in initiation (*dīkṣā*), it is stated in the *Yāmala*: "A place with marshy ground, deep, situated near a reservoir of long-standing water,
a fire-hall of those who maintain the sacred fires (*agnihotra*), a holy site, or one that is well-known."
O Pārvatī, these places— the abode of twice-born ones who observe their vows, or one's own hermitage— are highly praised for initiation.
One should not perform initiation in a dense grove, in a deep forest,
at the boundary of two regions, or in a vast wilderness frequented by predatory beasts.
In another tantra: "The banks of great rivers, the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, as well as celebrated sacred fords, holy fields, and hermitages [are suitable]."
All the forests and even all the mountains,
including the mountain cascades and the abodes of the deities on the hillsides.
In the *Mahākapilapañcarātra*:
"There, one who is expert in the science of architecture (*vāstu*) should examine the ground;
[avoiding] that which is cracked, contains debris, has anthills, or is overgrown with *rohiṇī* grass."
Ground that is far removed [from water] should be avoided, for it takes away the life and wealth of the builder;
ground that is cracked causes death, while saline soil destroys wealth.
It is always thorny, causes affliction, and is dangerous due to fear of enemies;
yet, when it flows toward the northeast corner, it certainly bestows prosperity upon the doer.
Land sloping toward the southeast destroys one's sons, longevity, and wealth;
land sloping toward the south constantly bestows fear of death.
That ground which has an inundation from the southwest (Nairṛta) causes the destruction of the household;
the earth said to have an inundation from the west (Varuṇa) causes the loss of wealth.
Land sloping toward the north-west always causes anxiety;
land sloping toward the east brings prosperity, while land sloping toward the north bestows boons.
30) In the *Gautamīyatantra*: "One should perform the ritual appropriation of the ground (bhūmi-parigraha) for as far as the sacred precinct (*āyatana*) extends;
that ground which is white clay is proclaimed to be *brāhmī*."
The earth with red soil is proclaimed as Kṣatriya, while that which is yellow is known as Vaiśya;
the black earth becomes Śūdra—thus it is described in four ways.
In the *Mahākapilapañcarātra*:
"The Brāhmaṇa ground is covered with *kuśa* grass; the Kṣatriya ground should be thick with *śara* grass;
the Vaiśya ground is thick with *kuśa* and *kāśa* grass; and the Śūdra ground is thick with all kinds of grass."
In the *Gautamīya Tantra*: "The Brāhmaṇī leads to the accomplishment of all aims; likewise, the Kṣatriyā bestows sovereignty;
the Vaiśyā brings wealth and grain; but the Śūdrā, O Sage, is censured."

In the *Prayogasāra*: "Having fashioned a cavity in the ground with a width of one *vitasti*, one should deposit those [remaining] clods of earth into it; when they have been placed therein, it is auspicious."
One should know that [the site] is middling in assemblies, while it is called inferior in small ones.
In the *Gautamīya Tantra*: "Then, one who is expert in the knowledge of architecture (*vāstu*) should examine the ground;
he should perform the purification of hidden obstacles (*śalya*) and the like, and should remove husks, charcoal, and other such debris."
If this is not performed, the practitioner (mantrin) shall obtain no fruit at all.
In the Mahākapila-pañcarātra:
"As long as water is being excavated, the defect of the *śalya* (impurity/obstruction) is destroyed."
Water situated far below cannot be dug up at all.
A pit five cubits deep should be dug for the pacification of the defects caused by the arrow;
then, having extracted the arrow, one should fill it back up so that it is perfectly level.
Having performed the sacrifice for the site on that ground, one should construct the pavilion.
Now, the procedure for the Vāstu sacrifice:
In the construction of a house or similar structures, wherever the deity of the site (Vāstudevatā) is not worshipped,
everything therein shall become void, destroyed by demons, obstacles, and the like.
Therefore, those desiring prosperity should properly perform the ritual worship of the site (*vāstvarcana*).
As stated in the *Mahākapila-pañcarātra*:
"First, during the acquisition of the ground, and likewise when laying the foundation stones..."
And for the purpose of constructing a water reservoir or a house, one should especially worship Vāstu.
In other rites as well, such as sacrifices and fire-offerings,
the Guru should prepare the Vāstu-maṇḍala by drawing it out with lines on a level surface.
31) In the Śāradā [Tantra]: "Having slain the Rākṣasa named Vāstu and having occupied his body, the fifty-three deities remain; one should first offer an oblation (bali) to them."

Somaśambhu states: In rituals of worship, one should visualize the Vāstu deity with its hands contracted and its form like that of an Asura, lying on its back; however, when constructing walls and so forth, it should be visualized with its face turned downwards.
His knees are joined to his elbows in the direction of the wind and fire;
his two feet are in the direction of the ancestors; his head is in the direction of Rudra; and his hands are joined in *añjali* at his heart.

In the *Gautamīya-tantra*: "Preceded by auspicious rites, with the blessings of Brahmins and the chanting of the Vedas, one should construct the mandala of Vāstu according to the prescribed rules and as it appears beautiful."
In the *Śāradā*: "One should lay down a thread extending from east to west, measuring one cubit;
then, taking a small point as a center within that, one should draw two fish-shapes on both sides."
One should lay down a thread situated between those two, extending from south to north;
likewise, one should draw crocodiles in the corners using each pair of outer points.
One should drop threads there with their tips positioned in the middle of the fish;
thus, a square shall arise, provided with four compartments.
Furthermore, the mantra-practitioner should divide that into sixty-four sections,
from Īśāna to Rākṣasa, and from Agni to Prabhañjana.
In this manner, being composed, one should apply two threads as the ear-thread.
One should first worship Brahmā in the center of the four squares;
thereafter, one should worship Ārya in the four directions, starting from the east.
Then [place] Vivasvat, Mitra, and Mahīdhara;
again, in the pairs of half-cells at the corners starting from the southeast (Agni), place them around [the periphery].
The wise one [should worship] Sāvitra and Savitṛ, Śakra and Indrajaya,
