it is the fire-wheel, O lady of excellent hips, that is hidden among all wheels. (375)
The fire consists of the nine planets, and those planets consist of fire;
therefore, having understood their abiding nature within the fire, one should perform the oblation (homa) in the fire.
I shall describe, according to the rules, the sequence of their positions among the lunar mansions during rites for pacification, nourishment, prosperity, and even those that are cruel:
the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Saturn, the Moon, and Mars.
Jīva, Rāhu, and Ketu—these nine, O Goddess, are the sky-goers (khecaras).
One should cause three and then three constellations, beginning with the Sun, to be given;
O Maheśvarī, one should count them until reaching the constellation of the Moon from the position of the Sun.
O Goddess, listen as I shall describe the results of the sun and the other planets in their proper order:
under the Sun there will be sorrow, and under Mercury there is the arrival of wealth.
One should know there is gain when Venus is [ascendant], and suffering when Saturn is, without a doubt;
there is gain when the Moon is, O Great Goddess, and indeed imprisonment when Mars is.
Through Guru there is the acquisition of wealth, and likewise through Rāhu there is loss;
through Ketu, death occurs—such, O Maheśvarī, is the fruit.
Having understood this, O Great Goddess, one should perform the rite of homa;
on whichever day the mouths of the gentle planets [are favorable], twenty oblations should be offered.

On that day, O Goddess, the commencement of the *saumya-homa* (auspicious oblation) is prescribed; likewise, the *krūra-homa* (fierce oblation) should take place at the onset of a fierce planetary influence.
Having understood this, O Great Goddess, one should perform the fire-sacrifice for specific desires;
otherwise, if performed incorrectly, it results in fruitlessness and self-destruction.
In the *Gaṇeśvaravimarśinī*, however, another specific detail is stated:
"Having drawn a grid of nine squares, one should place [the letters] of the asterisms in order within the two [squares] of the East and North-East;
[then] those of the West and North-West in the South and North."
Having placed the Sun and the others in the central square, one should predict the results;
with the Sun there will be wealth, and with Mercury there will be the acquisition of riches.
In the house of Venus, there shall be gain of wealth, but it may cause loss of progeny;
one should know that with the Moon there is profit, and with Mars, there is slaughter and imprisonment.
Jupiter brings about the gain of wealth, while Rāhu is considered to cause loss;
indeed, one always meets with death through Ketu in the Agnicakra.
376) One should count three by three from the solar asterism up to the state of the day;
the offerings should be made in the fire-pit (kuṇḍa) and on the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) by the most excellent preceptors.
In the case of obligatory (*nitya*) and occasional (*naimittika*) rites, such as the *durgā-homa* and others, one should not engage in deliberation.
In the *Brahmayāmala*: "Now I shall describe the stationing of the fire for the successful accomplishment of the acts of *homa*;
the King of Oblations (*havyarāj*) resides in the heavenly world, in the netherworld (*pātāla*), and upon the earth."
I shall describe that method for the benefit of practitioners.

Having combined the lunar day (tithi), the day of the week (vāra), the seven continents (saptadvīpa), and the four ages (caturyuga), one should divide by three; by the remainder, Pāvaka [is determined].
The Fire-god dwells in one [quarter] in heaven, in two in the netherworld (pātāla), and in the empty one in the world of mortals;
thus indeed does Pāvaka reside.
If the fire is situated in the heavenly realm (svargaloka), there is a portent; if situated in the netherworld (pātāla), there is loss of wealth;
but when the fire is situated in the mortal world (martyaloka), the oblation (homa) bestows the desired fruit.
Having understood this, the knower of mantras should perform the rite of homa.
Regarding the characteristics of the *sruk*, *sruva*, and fuel-sticks for the six rites, the Tantra states:
"The *sruk* and *sruva* should be made of gold in all auspicious rites."
These two, made of iron, should be used in rites such as the immobilization of others.

Peaceful rites (*śāntika*) should be performed in the worldly fire, and subjugation (*vaśya*) in the worldly fire; the rite known as immobilization (*stambhana*) occurs in the fire born from the *vaṭa* tree; enmity (*vidveṣa*) is to be known [as occurring] in the fire of the axle-wood (*akṣaśuc*), and it is remembered [to occur] in the cremation ground fire (*śmaśāna*) for the destruction of enemies (*kharbudha*).
These are declared as the six flaming rites for the purposes of eradication and killing;
for subjugation, pomegranate flowers are used, and for pacification, they should be with dūrvā grass.
For the rite of immobilization (stambhana), fuel-sticks made from the rājavṛkṣa tree and bathed in cow’s ghee are used;
for causing hatred (dveṣa), they are considered to be made from the kṣataruja tree and combined with the fat of a ewe.
For the rite of eradication (*uccāṭana*), [fuel sticks] produced from the *rasāla* tree combined with pungent oil are used;
for the rite of killing (*māraṇa*), those made of *khadira* wood combined with pungent oil are prescribed.
This is declared by practitioners of mantra to be the sacrificial substance (*homadravya*) for these six rites.
Likewise: through oblations of ghee, there is the acquisition of wealth; with white mustard seeds, supreme fame;
with *kiṃśuka* flowers, the attainment of all desires; and through oblations of fruit, happiness shall arise.

Affection is said to be gained through jaggery; through *campaka* and *pāṭala* flowers, one attains wealth (*ramā*); by offering oblations of sesame seeds, one obtains sons; and through *karavīra* flowers, women become submissive.
Dūrvā grass bestows longevity, and guḍūcī brings about the pacification of diseases;
sesame seeds are likewise said to do so, while through a homa of fragrant substances, good fortune is attained.
Through *śrīphala* fruits, *bilva* leaves, and likewise with water-born lotuses, one who has fallen from his kingdom shall regain his realm; the *mallikā* flower is considered to bestow fame.
By means of *karṇikāra* and *kiṃśuka* flowers, the gods shall be brought under control;
by means of *kāśamarda*, kings shall be submissive, and by means of *kṛtamāla*, the common people shall be brought under one's power.
Through *pāṭala* flowers, one may become a *śūdra*; through blue lotuses, one becomes *ramā*; through *jātī* flowers, one attains speech; and through sweet-smelling flowers, one gains desired wealth.
Through fuel-sticks of *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, or *plakṣa* wood, one attains one's desires;
through desired substances, one's wish is fulfilled, as is the case with barley and rice.
With *māṣa* beans, the enemies become mute; with *kodrava* grains, the occurrence of disease arises.
From the *kalāpa* oblation, a great fear will certainly come upon the enemies.
With fuel-sticks of *vibhītaka*, the family of enemies shall become insane;
with fuel-sticks of *śālmali*, the destruction of the enemy's wings will certainly occur.
Regarding the materials for the fire sacrifice (*homadravya*), the *Phetkāriṇītantra* states: "Now I shall describe the materials according to their respective rites:
in the rite of pacification (*śāntika*), however, they follow the sequence of milk, clarified butter, sesame seeds, and milk."
The creeper called Amṛtā is also prescribed there with milk-rice (pāyasa).
For nourishment (pauṣṭika), one should use bilva leaves; by using jasmine flowers (jātīpuṣpa), one becomes a king.
One desiring a daughter should offer oblations with parched grain (lāja), and likewise, one desiring prosperity (śrī) should use lotuses.
One obtains prosperity by offering curd, food by offering foods drenched in ghee,
and likewise by offering milk, clarified butter, or lotuses soaked in honey.
The mantra-practitioner should offer oblations with these prosperous substances for the pacification of great poverty;
through one hundred thousand homas of ghee, bilva, and sesame seeds, he shall obtain peace and a treasure-store.
For attraction, however, one should use salt, *priyaṅgu*, and *vilvaka* fruit;
or all of these together with *jātī* and *palāśa* flowers, or even each one individually.

One seeking subjugation should use *rājīlavaṇaka* (salt with stripes) for subjugation, or those substances prescribed for nourishing rites (*pauṣṭika*); for the purpose of attraction, one should use *jātī* flowers, and for summoning (*ākṛṣṭi*), those produced from *karavīra*.
Desiring the death of an enemy, the practitioner of mantra should combine cotton, neem, and human hair smeared with buttermilk, or even those alone, and offer them as oblations.
378) Or, for the purpose of slaying an enemy, one should perform the homa with mustard oil;
or a person should offer oblations in the excrement with *rohī* seeds mixed with sesame.
In all rites of malevolent magic (abhicāra), one should offer oblations of seeds mixed with chaff and thorns, as well as cotton-seeds, clarified butter, and sesame seeds.
With the cruel feathers of crows and owls, karaskara and vibhitaka fruits,
marica, mustard seeds, prepared with the milky sap of arka and the three pungents (katutraya).
In the rite of killing (*māraṇa*), one should employ pungent oils and the milky sap of the *snuhī* plant.
In a fire-oblation intended for the destruction of an enemy, by offering oblations into the ears and other parts of the fire, the enemy's ears and other parts are destroyed. As it has been said:
"Upon the head of the fire, at its base, in its ears, or likewise in its eyes..."
If one should offer oblations, then the enemy there will be swiftly destroyed.
The characteristics of the fire, such as its color and other signs, have already been stated previously. Likewise:
"One desiring long life [should offer] ghee, sesame seeds, dūrvā grass, and mango sprouts;
by means of mango leaves smeared with milk, one shall instantly destroy fever."
Guḍūcī is for conquering death as well as for pacification;
likewise, with white mustard seeds, one who offers oblations may immediately remove disease from a fever patient.
Desiring rain, one obtains nourishment by offering fuel-sticks of *vetasī* and its leaves;
by offering *putrañjīva* seeds, one obtains a son;
and through an oblation of ghee and *guggulu*, one attains mastery over speech.
With jasmine, great-flowered jasmine, and blossoms produced from the nāga and punnāga trees.
With flowers, there is the accomplishment of Sarasvatī as well as the fulfillment of all aims;
with milk or salt, one should offer oblations for the warding off of rain.
With red flowers, apāmārga, aṅkola, and subhadraka— these,
combined with sweet substances, the practitioner of mantras should perform the rite of subjugation.
By means of dry leaves stirred up by the wind, wood fallen by lightning,
a camel bone, or charcoal, the eradication of an enemy shall occur.
A wise person should perform a rite for peace using dūrvā grass, guḍūcī, and cow's ghee; with sesame seeds and rice; with food offerings; and with palāśa wood fuel.
In another tantra it is said: "For gentle rites, turmeric mixed with water is prescribed;
hot water with black pepper shall be used for killing and paralyzing."
Water mixed with the blood of a ram is prescribed for the rites of hatred and eradication;
this is declared as the substance for libation by those who have reached the further shore of the Āgamas.
One who knows the mantras, sitting comfortably during an auspicious rite, should perform the libation;
for the rite of immobilization (stambhana), the libation should be performed while kneeling upon the ground.
The foremost of practitioners should satisfy [the deity] with a single foot [of water] when starting with aversion;
for subjugation and pacification, a golden vessel is prescribed, while an earthen vessel is considered suitable for immobilization.
For causing enmity, a vessel made of khadira wood; for expulsion, one fashioned from iron;
for killing, it should be a hen's egg—these are the vessels used in the rite of libation.

Thus are the seven other applications. Now follows the specific application according to the *Pheravīya*: one who desires knowledge should offer oblations of sesame and clarified butter mixed with honey.
In the *Siddhasārasvata*: by offering oblations of *bandhūka* flowers, one makes kings behave like servants;
and by offering oblations of ghee and salt, one attracts a beloved woman.
By performing oblations with *vakula* blossoms, a man obtains good fortune;
by using *mallikā*, *jāti*, *punnāga*, and *kadamba* flowers, he shall attain nourishment.
Furthermore, by performing a fire sacrifice with sandalwood, agallochum, saffron, and camphor,
the practitioner of the mantra of Nīlasarasvatī shall obtain all desired objects.
By performing a fire-oblation with the flowers of the *rājavṛkṣa* tree, one shall obtain prosperity;
having worshipped [the deity] with bilva leaves mixed with ghee while reciting the root mantra.
By offering a thousand oblations every day, one attains the supreme goal;
through the homa of *mālatī* flowers smeared with ghee, one becomes a swift poet.
In the Surendrasaṃhitā: "One desiring knowledge should offer lotuses soaked in honey; by offering sesame seeds smeared with the three sweets, one indeed becomes like Vaiśravaṇa in wealth."
The wise one should offer eight hundred oblations of red flowers smeared with the three sweets;
kings will come under his control within half a moment, without a doubt.
By performing oblations with *tagara* flowers smeared with milk for as long as a year, day after day, using a thousand *vilva* leaves, one shall obtain great poetic skill.
One who eats sacrificial food (haviṣya) with hair unbound shall recite [the mantra] ten thousand times and attain the supreme goal, which is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
His speech in the assembly became composed of both prose and verse;
having purified himself, he recited the Padmāvatī mantra one thousand times.
380) One should offer an oblation at a crossroads; he will certainly become a swift messenger.
By merely reciting [the mantra] a hundred times, a man [should apply] a mark with yellow pigment (rocanā).
Having performed this, the mantra-practitioner brings whoever he beholds under his control like a servant;
beginning before sunrise, he should recite the mantra until sunset.
For twenty-one days, one should offer a bali-oblation at night in the palace;
one should utter the word "kahakaha" and then the word "kālike."
Having uttered the word *piśāci*, one should give the offering with the mantra: "Take the *piṇḍa*, *dviṭha* twice.
By giving the *bali* in this manner, the practitioner becomes omniscient.
But in the Matsyasūkta it is said: "One desiring knowledge should offer oblations of milk-rice mixed with honey;
one desiring wealth should offer oblations of sesame and clarified butter mixed with honey."
The rule for the fire sacrifice (homa) stated in the Tantra extends up to ten thousand repetitions;
it is performed with ten thousand bilva leaves combined with the three sweets.
There is no doubt that from this oblation (havana) all forms of speech arise;
by performing one hundred thousand homas with its leaves, one becomes the Lord of Wealth himself, accompanied by Śrī.
By means of an oblation of red sandalwood, a man becomes omniscient;
by means of an oblation of white sandalwood, he becomes a literal Indra upon earth.
By means of a homa of red sandalwood, one becomes truly Bṛhaspati on earth;
by a homa of a hundred thousand barley grains, one [attains this] whether the land has been consecrated or unconsecrated.
Having mastered all languages, one becomes omniscient before long;
one explains even those scriptures not previously heard—of this there is no doubt.
Through the oblation of *śāla* wood, fish, and other substances, one is considered a representative of Śiva;
O Goddess of the Gods, one hundred thousand oblations should be offered with sesame seeds and clarified butter.
The practitioner certainly becomes a master who has reached the further shore of all sciences,
by means of the threefold recitation of the Vidyā together with the Mātṛkā at dawn.
And by drinking [this], the practitioner shall attain all sciences within just one month;
having arisen during the final watch of the night, he should assume the Kuṇḍalinī posture.
A man who meditates upon Ugratārā shall indeed become a partaker of liberation;
for the sake of pacification, the best of practitioners should meditate on her as white as a kunda flower or the moon.
One should worship her, radiant with a smoky luster, in the wind mandala; thus worshipped, she undoubtedly maddens the strength and intellect of one's enemies.

In the *Surendrasaṃhitā*: "One should worship the bliss of nectar arising from the *kula* and *akula*, which is equal to ten million suns and situated within the enclosure (*vāṭa*) at the center of the thread (*sūtra*)."
One should worship by offering the nectar of the Kula arising from the union of the Liṅga and the Yoni;
likewise, one worships the Kula in the Liṅga through the firm binding of Kuṇḍalinī.
One should worship in the center of the support-lotus, which has two feet and is the abode of the two-footed;
in the sixteen-spoked liṅga, and in the twelve-spoked maṇipūraka.

One should worship the Goddess in the heart, which has ten petals; in the throat, which has twelve half-petals (six); in the forehead, which has four petals; and in the area crowded with the tongue and the palate.
A man devoted to celibacy within a white chamber should worship the Goddess with white offerings and cloths wrapped as veils.
One should perform the rite in this manner with white offerings such as curd, milk, rice,
and so forth, or through mental resolves (saṅkalpa), and then meditate upon the supreme Vāgīśvarī.
Moving along the path of Brahman by means of the sequence of piercing the *liṅgas*,
[one attains] the divine nectar situated in the emission, which arises like a stream of milk.
Having drunk the nectar of the Kula there, one should enter the Kula once again;
one should go to the Kula once more and cause it to rest in the dvādaśānta.
In the thousand-petaled great lotus is the Vāgbhava syllable, like the full moon;
then, having pierced the Brahma-knot, one bestows [the nectar] with seven or eight streams.
One should cause the uvula to enter the root of the palate by way of the Brahma-path,
having filled the tongue with that Vidyā which has the form of the letters of the Mātṛkā.
One should visualize the external form and color as having the appearance of a lamp at the tip of the tongue;
likewise, situated at the tip of the tongue, it extends from the root up to the aperture of Brahmā.
One should contemplate the Great Vidyā, beginning with the syllable Vāgbhava, in the form of a lamp,
[located] in the two hands, the two feet, and likewise in the three channels (nāḍīs).
Having raised Vāgīśī from the foundation (ādhāra), one should lead her to the twelfth [center];
taking the foundation as the twelfth, one should pierce that knot.
Therefore, having brought it to the tip of the tongue, one should contemplate it in the form of a lamp;
by reciting this one hundred thousand times, one shall burn away all sins.
Then, having known all that is moving and unmoving, one attains omniscience;
thereafter, by reciting the Great Vidyā, a person becomes a lord of speech.
In the assembly of debate, she was a pillar of speech that paralyzed the opponents; her splendor eclipsed the pride and brilliance of the gathered host of scholars.

One who understands the essence of the seven types of reasoning, the meaning of words and sentences, and verbal ornaments, becomes a true poet— even if previously mute— merely by placing this [work] upon their tongue.
One who discerns the essence of verbal ornaments that are exceedingly delicate and expansive should employ them like rows of ocean waves tossed by the wind.
With feet and ankles [marked by these signs], one shall become a composer of the most excellent mahākāvyas;
his intellect shall be unimpeded in the treatises, like that of Vācaspati, and he shall achieve victory.
Within three days, one should write upon the tongue of the child with a golden stylus, using honey and white dūrvā grass.
One should write the Vidyā beginning with Vāgbhava, having worshipped it and recited its mantra;
he alone is a wise and illustrious man, and never a fool.
Having written this Vāgīśvarī-vidyā upon the head of a child and placed his hand [thereon], a man should recite the vidyā one hundred and eight times;
he too composes all verses without exception, just like the Lord of Speech.
In the *Vīracūḍāmaṇi*: "In all rites, milk-rice (*pāyasa*) and the finest fruits [are used];
by the oblation of blue lotuses (*nīlotpala*), a man becomes a master of speech."
By offering oblations of hibiscus flowers, all accomplishments are produced;
by means of an oblation of hibiscus flowers, a deer-eyed woman shall be brought under one's control.

With *mālatī* flowers one gains great wisdom; with *kadamba* flowers, black sandalwood [is attained]; with red lotuses, *Mahālakṣmī*; and with *campaka* flowers, for the purpose of paralyzing (*stambhana*). One should offer beautiful *bilva* leaves in rites for pacification (*śāntika*).
By the mere offering of sesame seeds into the fire, one is liberated from all sins;
by the offering of *dūrvā* grass, one attains long life, and by offerings of reeds (*vetasa*), one becomes a bringer of rain.
The diligent practitioner should perform the fire-oblation with coconuts eight times;
in his home, prosperity shall remain firm, and kings will follow him like servants.
The Goddess is satisfied in an instant by an oblation of plantain fruits;
with wood-apples and citron fruits, there is the destruction of all diseases.
With *vibhītaka* and *nimba*, one kills an enemy in an instant.
[One should also use] snake venom, *rājila* salt, black pepper, asafoetida, and *arka*-derived [substances].
383) For the purpose of killing and for malevolent rites (abhicāra), each respective substance is prescribed;
[these include] fruits, flowers, and so forth, one by one, and grapes (drākṣā) as the fifth.
Guggulu is equal to a jujube fruit; kapittha is remembered as being threefold;
mātuliṅga is fourfold; and sesame seeds are remembered as being a hundredfold.
According to the measurement of Mārīca,
one should take thirty-two units each of camphor, saffron, mustard seed, and black mustard.
One karṣa of salt, four guñjās of asafoetida,
and one karṣa of ghee— this is said to be the same as milk.
One śukti of curd, one pala of coriander (dhānyaka),
thirty finger-breadths of dūrvā grass, and twelve finger-breadths of vetasa.
In the accomplishment of pacification, subjugation, and so forth, all substances should be combined with the three sweets;
for killing, expulsion, and the like, they should be saturated with pungent oil.
One should offer ten thousand oblations of the flesh of the kaukkura, the ruru deer, the goat, and likewise the buffalo into the sacrificial pit; one will then become like Vaiśravaṇa in wealth.
The flesh of a pigeon, a vulture, an owl, a crow, a cock,
and a jackal is prescribed for the rite of malevolent incantation (abhicāra).
In the *Vīratantra*: "He who meditates upon Tāriṇī, resembling a lamp-flame, upon his tongue—his poetic skill, equal to that of Bṛhaspati, will be composed like that of Śukra."

In the *Nīlatantra*: "Having risen during the *brāhma-muhūrta*, having performed the necessary duties and being well-restrained, the wise one should meditate on the Vidyā in the form of light upon the tongue and recite it."
His speech shall flow like nectar and become effective in every way.
In the *Ekavīrākalpa*: "Having visualized the Vidyā in the form of a lamp upon the tongue at dawn, one should drink water after reciting the Vidyā together with the Mātṛkā three times."
By following the prescribed method for drinking water, even a mute may become a skilled poet.
In the Matsyasūkta: "Merely by meditating upon [the mantra] on the tongue, a man becomes a knower of the three periods of time;
that best of practitioners who meditates upon the Vidyā without making any distinction [between them]."
He becomes liberated while living and is certainly liberated at the end;
the propitiation of the Goddess with honey bestows the fruits of all desires.

One who subsists on sacrificial food (haviṣya) with hair unbound should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times with devotion; this directly bestows the eight supernatural powers and destroys even the greatest sins.
384) His speech shall become entirely composed of both prose and verse.

In the *Siddhasārasvata* [tantra]: by merely reciting [the mantra] one hundred times, a person who applies a tilaka of *rocanā* (cow bezoar) and becomes a master of the mantra will bring whoever he looks upon under his control like a servant.
Regarding the attainment of the body (*dehasiddhi*), it is stated in the *Matsyasūkta*:
the Goddess said—
O Blessed One, knower of all truths, benefactor of the world!
By what means, O Lord of Gods, is the perfection of the body produced?
Tell me that, O Omniscient One, if you have affection for me.
Īśvara said:
O Goddess, who are easily accessible through devotion, I shall tell you the remedy;
this must not be disclosed anywhere, for it is difficult to find even in the three worlds.
One should grind a maiden who holds an umbrella together with black gram.
If one anoints the body at dawn with the milk of cows of a single color and the juice of the seed of the plantain tree, the attainment of subjugation (*vaśya*) occurs.
One should eat the root of white aparājitā with honey;
by applying it on a day of the sun, white leprosy is destroyed.
One should grind the fruit and flower of the *aśoka* together with the fruits of the *eraṇḍa* on the previous day, and consume it on the following day.
No disease arising from wind or indigestion occurs in his body.
In the *Phetkāriṇītantra*: "In a deep pond, when the sun is seized by darkness (at night), one should quickly and with effort bring a wooden staff [into the water] and cause it to be drawn out."
With that very same honey-smeared [substance], one should write the root mantra, which bestows success, within a circle of vajras upon a lotus leaf.
At the conclusion of the *māyā*, the best of practitioners should say, "Make so-and-so [mine]";
then, having cast [the substance] into that square sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), he should also perform the fire-oblation (*homa*).
Having first uttered the *praṇava*, one should [offer] a lotus with true petals, moistened with milk and water, possessing the red luster of lotuses, and likewise a pair of lotuses.
One should utter the word "Mahāpadme," then the word "Padmāvati," followed by the mantra "Hūṃ Hūṃ Svāhā," and thus offer the bali offering as before.
Thus, whoever performs this rite shall certainly become a swift poet.
Then, at midnight, one should always offer a bali-oblation at a crossroads.
Having first inscribed the Praṇava and then Hṛllekhā thereafter,
one should utter the word "Mahā" at the end of the word "Ekajaṭe."
Then, having addressed the Lord of Yakṣas and the Lord [of the North],
and having uttered the word "approached" twice, I said, "Accept the offering."
Having uttered "grahāpaya" twice, then say "mama sarva," followed by the word "śāntiṃ kuru," and immediately thereafter the Paravidyā.
One should say, "Draw it in two ways," and likewise, "Split! Cut in two! Then, by means of the word, one should bring the entire world under control.
This mantra, "māyā svāhā," bestows prosperity and success in rites such as the offering of oblations (bali);
it destroys enemy armies, planetary afflictions, misfortunes, diseases, malevolent spells (kṛtyā), and the like.
In the *Nīlatantra*: "If this bali-mantra is employed, it shall accomplish all ritual applications.
Therefore, when midnight has passed, one should always offer the bali at a crossroads."
It destroys enemy armies, seizing spirits, portents, diseases, and malevolent spells;
having first uttered the Praṇava, one should then recite "Ugratāre."
One should utter "Vikaṭadaṃṣṭre" twice, followed by "kṣobhaya" (or "mohaya") twice;
then one should say "khādya" twice, and likewise "paca" twice.
Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Destroy those who are intent on harming me, as well as those intent on reviling me, together with the assembly of yoginīs! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

"Paravidyām ākarṣaya chedaya svāhā! Kapile gṛhṇa gṛhṇa svāhā! Thus it is said in the *Phetkāriṇī*. Alternatively, on the tongue of the child, one should first draw [the mantra] with a golden stylus using honey and parched grain (*madhulāja*) prior to the cutting of the umbilical cord.
The mantra-practitioner should write the root mantra with white dūrvā grass upon the lips of one [for whom it is intended];
by the utterance of that speech, the child shall become eloquent and a swift poet.
In the *Mahogratārākalpa* and the *Matsyasūkta*:
"When a son is born, the rite of birth-consecration (*janmasaṃskāra*) is immediately praised;
one should write the mantra upon his tongue with a splinter of sacrificial wood (*yajñadāru*)."
Having worshipped three times with the right hand alone,
one should recite the mantra for each and form a very beautiful row.
First, the consecration (saṃskāra) should be performed; at its conclusion, one should write down the mantra.
Then, one should worship the auspicious Tāriṇī with perfumes, sandalwood, and flowers.
Facing north, one should place the supreme pedestal and worship the goddess Tāriṇī with various most beautiful offerings of food.
One's son shall become a poet and an eloquent speaker, truthful and with senses subdued;
one should diligently write the mantra with kuśa-root and honey.
Either the father’s brother, or again the mother’s brother, or even the father himself should write the mantra; never anyone else at all.
Furthermore, O Goddess, one should install the mantra which bestows the fruits of all desires, so that the brother may always be praiseworthy and foremost.
Having placed the child on his mother’s lap and carefully strewn darbha grass,
he, joined by the practitioners, should perform a rite for the child’s peace.
Then, one should perform the hymn of praise at the mother’s left ear. Now, the hymn:
O Mother Goddess, salutations to you, O sinless one who bears the form of Brahman.
Out of compassion, remove my obstacles and grant me the accomplishment of the mantra.
O Maheśī, O boon-granting Goddess, whose form is supreme bliss!
Out of compassion, remove my obstacles and bestow upon me the perfection of mantra.
O Kaumāri, sovereign of all vidyās, supreme in youthful play,
out of compassion remove my obstacles and grant me the accomplishment of the mantra.
O Goddess who bears the form of Viṣṇu, O rider of the great Garuḍa!
Out of compassion, remove my obstacles and grant me the perfection of mantra.
O Vārāhī, O boon-granting Goddess, who lifted the earth with Your tusk!
Out of compassion, remove my obstacles and grant me the perfection of the mantra.
O Goddess who bears the form of Śakra, worshipped by Śakra and the other gods,
please remove my obstacles and grant me the accomplishment of the mantra.
O Cāmuṇḍā, adorned with a garland of severed heads and blood, O destroyer of obstacles!
Out of compassion, remove my obstacles and grant me the perfection of mantra.
O Mahālakṣmī, you of great energy, destroyer of great disturbances!
Out of compassion, remove my obstacles and grant me the perfection of the mantra.
O Goddess, who consists of both the measurer and the measured, yet is beyond the measurer and the measured;
O Goddess, who are one and yet manifold, whose form is the universe—salutations be to you!
Whoever, being self-restrained, recites this hymn at the commencement of undertakings,
or upon seeing a flash of lightning, no obstacle shall arise for him.

Having praised [the deity] and recited the great mantra, one should then feed the Brāhmaṇas. The Goddess said: "O Lord, what is the substance for cleansing the tongue? What is the protection for the body? What is the protection for the son, and what is the medicine for the protection of the house?"
O God, I desire to hear it; please tell me out of your grace.
Īśvara said: Having applied the root of Kṛṣṇājayantī and the root of Apāmārga to the tongue on the sixth day, [one obtains] a son.
One should know that the root of white aparājitā, the southern bark of the arka tree,
and the protective substances prepared on one's birth day constitute the protective materials.
One should place a piece of bamboo, the root of a lotus, a dried cow, and a human skull in the northern direction;
then there will be no fear whatsoever.
One should wear the bark of the Jambu tree and the leaves of the Shimbi plant on the head of those who have been born;
thus there is no fear of Rākṣasas, nor of diseases, sorcery, and the like.
Having planted a *pippala* tree at the four corners of the house,
one should station it outside at the entrance and bind there a goat and a monkey.
On the night of the sixth day, two roots of the *rambhā* plant will sprout;
one should place the sword right there, as well as a very handsome Brahmin.
Having established an elderly woman or a humble brother-in-law [to hold the child],
one should then bathe the Kumāra with the natural juice of the Jayantī plant itself.
One should sprinkle [the tree] with a mixture of *jayantī* ghee and water;
having established it upon an eight-petaled [diagram], that person shall become wise and possessed of sons.
Having diligently obtained the root and bark of the Nāgeśvara tree,
one should grind them into a powder, mix it with ghee, and then prepare a wick.
Having prepared a lamp, the knower of mantras should sever the channel of the son;
thus the son shall become well-disciplined, intelligent, and endowed with virtues.
And one should place the bark of the southern *aśoka* tree at the entrance;
having placed these, one should then place the bark of the *jambu* tree together with its hair.
For one who always places [this] at the door, there shall be the destruction of obstacles;
having worshipped Tāriṇī on the night of the thirteenth lunar day.
Holding an Arka bark in his hand, he should touch the Tāriṇī stone;
directing his intent toward his desire with diligence, he attains it—of this there is no doubt.
Holding the root of a mango tree in his hand, whoever should touch the Tāriṇī mantra—
especially on the thirteenth lunar day— shall obtain the fruit of all desires.
The mantra of touch for the *kulluka* and the *tāramāra*, O bestower of supreme bliss:
"O Supreme Goddess, protect me in this terrible, difficult-to-cross cycle of existence!"
O destroyer of all sins, O you who annihilate every evil,
O you whose form is the consciousness of the supreme moment— protect me, O Supreme Goddess!
In the *Phetkāriṇītantra*: "Having taken charcoal from a cremation ground on a Tuesday at night, one should wrap it in a black cloth and bind it with a red thread."
Having consecrated it one hundred times with mantras, one should cast it into the house of the enemy;
within seven days, this will effect their great expulsion.
One should write the mantra upon human bone with turmeric mixed with milk; having recited it one thousand times at night on a Sunday.
In whosever house it is thrown, death shall occur within three months;
in the field there will be loss of crops, and in the horse, a loss of speed.

There will be loss of wealth in the house of wealth, and its total depletion in the middle of the village; moreover, there will be great hatred toward those named after one's enemies or those who hate him.
Now, regarding the heroic applications (*vīraprayoga*) in the *Gandharva-tantra*: "If one gazes daily at a menstruating woman on the earth for a thousand [times],
then the debater, his established doctrine destroyed, shall enter the surface of the earth."
Placing his hand upon the mountain, free from fear and with a disciplined mind,
he too attains poetic inspiration and goes to the state of immortality.
In the *Nīlatantra*: "The supreme practitioner, encircled by the great trees and creepers of Cīna, if he recites the mantra at night, she herself becomes a wish-fulfilling creeper."
If it is encircled by creepers according to the number [of days] in the sequence of lunar dates (tithi),
then accomplishment shall be attained within a month through a thousand recitations.
If it is recited twice as much on the eighth and fourteenth days,
then at that very moment there is great accomplishment, difficult even for the gods to attain.
Having written the seed-syllable with saffron upon a great Chinese tree,
and having inscribed the name of the person to be acted upon beside it, one should strike it with glances and showers [of mantras].
Afflicted by desire, she goes there where the practitioner resides;
having prepared a bolus smeared with the juice of the great *cīna* tree.
O Goddess, he in whose name an offering is given deserves death before long;
[if it is offered] with bilva leaves sprinkled with the juice of the flowers of the great Cīna tree.
Having worshipped the Goddess a thousand times in the cremation ground, the best of practitioners then attains a kingdom, provided that she does not flee.
And even the fruit obtained from being entwined by the great trees and creepers of China—
the celestial nymphs do not equal even a sixteenth part of that merit.
Entering a house of creepers yields fruit exceeding that of a corpse-seat;
O Goddess, a practitioner who is always such as this is rare on earth.

O Goddess, by revealing this, death occurs; it is not otherwise. Or else, having looked at the lower part [of the body], or at the circle of the breasts, or having placed the hand in the middle of the womb, one should recite the mantra.
Beginning from the time of the menstrual period until the next such period occurs,
by reciting [the mantra] during that interval, one becomes free from all affliction and a master of all accomplishments.
Having performed the transference, one should carry out here the ritual applications (prayoga) taught in the Kālikā-mantra-tantras;
likewise, one should properly perform there as well the applications taught herein.
In the *Phetkāriṇītantra*: "The knower of mantras should write [the diagram] upon a pair of yonis on birch bark with lac resin;
then, in the center of that, he should write the king of mantras joined with the name of the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*)."
Then, one should write the six long vowels, excluding the neuter (ḷ), within the hexagon;
on the eight petals, the eight syllables; and outside of that, two enclosures of walls (bhūpura).
O lady of excellent vows, the most eminent practitioner should draw the eight divisions and the earth-fortress (bhūpura) upon a golden plate,
a birch bark, or even one made of silver.
One should draw [the design] with a golden stylus combined with the eight fragrances,
or alternatively, one may write it with a stalk of dūrvā grass or with the root of kuśa grass.
Wrapped in yellow cloth, one should encase it in lac;
it should be bound with a silk thread as an ornament for the necks of children.
On the left arm of women and on the right arm of others;
by this, a barren woman obtains a son, and a poor man becomes wealthy.
This protection was formerly established by Gautama and others for the sake of knowledge,
and by other kings desiring victory in battle for the sake of triumph.

Regarding the "eight syllables": the Vāgbhava, the Kuladevī, the Tāraka, and likewise the Vāgbhava; then the Hṛllekhā and the Astra-mantra, ending with the Vahnijāyā (Svāhā)—this is declared the supreme eight-syllabled mantra, said to be the essence of all mantras.
This means the letters of the mantra as they have been stated.
Now, regarding the yantra, in the Rudrayāmala: "Now I shall describe the yantra; listen, O beloved of Hara."
One should place a triangle lotus encircled by a hexagon.
One should then provide a great eight-petaled yantra, followed by the three principles (tritattva), and then three enclosures of the earth (bhūpura) provided with the eight spikes (vasuśūla).
The preceptor should carefully place the syllables *ṭhaṃ* and *vaṃ* conjoined at the throat;
this is declared to be the Yantra by the grace of Sarasvatī.
At the base of the petals, a pair of vowels is prescribed; on the petals, the eight groups of consonants (vargas) are remembered.
In its opening is the Gāyatrī, and in the triangle is the syllable of the mantra.
The wise one should write the name of the person to be accomplished (sādhya), joined with the genitive case-ending.
Likewise, one should draw the previously mentioned yantra provided with four petals,
either on cow-dung or on white sandalwood paste.
O Maheśvarī, one should draw the yantra with a needle made of gold, silver, coral, or any other precious material.
One should specify that the probe (śalākā) measures four finger-breadths;
one should fashion the probe to be well-clothed and truly beautiful.
Then, the wise one should write the syllable *hrīṃ* upon a lotus vessel on the eastern petal; he should write *strīṃ* on the right [southern] petal, and then write *phaṃ* on the western petal.
The wise one should write "ṬAṂ" in the north and "HŪṂ" in the center;
O Goddess of the Gods, this yantra has been taught by Akṣobhya.
One should tie it with a silk cloth as an ornament for the necks of children;
likewise, it should be worn on the left hand by women and on the right hand by men.
Even a barren woman obtains a son, and one who is destitute shall obtain wealth;
this protection was formerly bound by Gautama and others for the sake of knowledge.
For the sake of fame, other kings desiring victory in battle [rely on this],
yet in the three worlds there is nothing equal to it for the purification of knowledge and speech.
Now, for the purpose of the yantra, the Tārākavaca— the armor-mantra as taught in the Gandharvatantra— is written.
Bhairavī said:
This secret which is proclaimed as supreme, the universal deliverer within the Tārīṇī,
is the armor named *Tryailokyavijaya*, the very embodiment of mantra.
O Bhairava, out of compassion, please speak for the benefit of practitioners regarding that which is honored by the six traditions and endowed with the six groups of six.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the armor (*kavaca*) named *Tryailokyavijaya*, which brings happiness to practitioners and is the very embodiment of mantra.
Holding which, the heroic Lord Viṣṇu repeatedly conquered the Dānavas;
that Acyuta, the imperishable one, destroys those who are strengthened by their austerities.
By whose grace the Lord Brahmā performs creation,
and by whose grace Śiva formerly destroyed the three cities;
By means of which Indra, his prowess obstructed, slew Vṛtra when protected;
by which even Agni is difficult to overcome, and Yama, the King of Dharma, is invincible.
Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kuvera, Īśvara, and the others—
by worshipping [him] with even a tenth part [of their own power], they destroy enemies in battle.
By whose instruction Skanda, the commander-in-chief of the inhabitants of heaven,
slew the fierce one named Tāraka and other exceedingly arrogant Daityas.
Having known which, the immensely radiant Rāma Bhārgava conquered the Kṣatriyas in battle— though they were strengthened by boons— and subsequently gratified the goddess Kālikā.
The Lord, together with his attendants, [was gratified] by the flesh arising from the bodies of the Kṣatriyas and their blood—
the flesh and blood by which Vyāsa and other sages composed the Mahābhārata and other works.
The Lord Bhava, the omniscient Vivasvat of exceeding splendor, triumphs over the world as the bodiless one;
he is the moon that brings joy to the universe.
O Bhairavī, hear from me as it has been told by Śaṅkara how Time measures everything through its power.
To Skanda, the cause of the mass of inauspiciousness for the worlds of the gods,
that [teaching] was formerly proclaimed by him to the wise Paraśurāma.
By the command of the illustrious Lord Śaṅkara, the Great Master,
I shall relate that to you, O Goddess of Devas, exactly as it was obtained by the High-Souled One.
Once, for the protection of the gods, Kārttikeya, who was eager for battle,
[was present] in the delightful Nandana grove, adorned with various flowers.
Resounding with the cries of warbling cuckoos, swarms of bees, and peacocks,
and radiant with the beauty of lotuses, water-lilies, white lilies, and hundred-petaled roses.

Having prostrated before the Lord who is half-female (Ardhanārīśvara), who was seated upon a beautiful divine throne beneath a *pārijāta* tree and served by a gentle breeze fragrant, cool, and blissful, Guha spoke.
Kārttikeya said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, you who bestow grace upon your devotees!
You are the Creator, you are the Father, O Lord; you alone are the granter of victory.
You alone are the goal of those who seek a refuge; you are consciousness, the supreme intellect.
You are indeed the destination of both the high and the low; O All-pervading Lord, you alone are my shelter.
Bhairava said:
When he had thus petitioned Girīśa, the Lord of the Gods,
Pārvatī, seated upon his chest, spoke out of compassion.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Blessed One, Lord of all gods, destroyer of the enemies of all gods, omnipresent one;
you alone are the Lord of all worlds, the eternal witness of all.
This very young prince, whose limbs are delicate and who is dear to me, has been consecrated by you for the protection of the gods; he is the one who rides upon the peacock.

O Lord, quickly instruct him in that by which he may be protected and conquer his enemies— that by which he may master the illusions of the Asuras, the gods, the Gandharvas, and those of human origin.
Neither yakṣas nor vidyādharas, nor rākṣasīs or dānavīs, can harm him with their deceptive illusions or weapons; act in such a way.
Bhairava said: Thus entreated by his beloved, the illustrious Lord Śaṅkara,
out of compassion, spoke the armor (kavaca) that bestows the fruits of the four aims of human life.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
O Great Goddess, there exists a secret armor (kavaca) equal to the Veda, belonging to Tāriṇī, who is the embodiment of Brahman; it delivers men from even the most terrible calamities.
O Goddess, this armor named Trailokyavijaya is the embodiment of mantra; it consists of all powers and is the crusher of all misfortunes.
Bestowing all desires and withering the hearts of all enemies—Oṃ; for this Tryailokyavijaya, Akṣobhya is said to be the Ṛṣi.
The meter is Anuṣṭubh, the deity is the Goddess Śrī, and the goddess is Mattogratāriṇī;
Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable, Trīṃ is the supreme power (parā-śakti), and Hūṃ is known as the pinning-stake (kīlaka).
The application (viniyoga) is proclaimed for one desiring victory over such-and-such; and for a man who knows the Kullukā-mantra, [the goddesses] become intent on carrying out his commands.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the other gods, as well as all the siddhis;
likewise Māheśvarī, Bhayaṅkarī, and Nārasiṃhī.
The *kullukas* of Mahogrā are hidden in all tantras:
Vāsudeva, Hara, Brahmā, Tāriṇī, and Prakṛti are always [the deities].
The single form is always to be contemplated; indeed, the single form is established.
Having joined that glorious form from the top to the bottom at the central region, one should meditate upon it.
The Kullukā is the manifold practice, each always consisting of three syllables;
she is renowned as Māheśvarī, the illustrious Kullukatāriṇī.

May she, who possesses the luster of a great cloud, who is dark-complexioned, and endowed with sixteen arms, eternally protect [me] from above for the attainment of the fruits of the four aims of life.
One should meditate upon her holding a sword and a knife, clad in yellow garments, seated upon a corpse;
likewise, one should contemplate the Praṇava, Bhuvaneśvarī, Ananta and the others, and Śiva.
Within that is the seed-syllable of Kūrma, conjoined with Bindu and Nāda;
followed by "Homage to Tārā," and the pair "tāraya tāraya" (save, save) for all those who are difficult to rescue.
This [mantra] ending in *svāhā* belongs to the terrifying Śrīmad-Bhuvanatarī;
she is dark-complexioned, has twelve arms, wears red garments, and sits upon a corpse.
One should constantly meditate upon the Eternal One (Nityā), who holds a sword and a dagger, within the lotus of the heart;
[reciting] the Kūrca, Nṛsiṃha, Kroṃ, Kūrca, Lajjā, Astra, and Kūrcaka.
She is renowned as Nārasiṃhī, the glorious savior from distress;
she is dark-complexioned, ten-armed, holding a sword and a chisel in her hands, and seated upon a corpse.
One should always meditate upon her who dwells in the *mūlādhāra*, clad in white garments.
Oṃ, may Kullukatāriṇī, with the syllable *hsauṃ*, constantly protect my head.
May the goddess Kalahrīṃ, who is the deliverer of Brahmā, protect my topknot;
may Hasastrīṃ Vajratāriṇī protect the right side of my head.
May Vaṃ Sahūṃ Durgatāriṇī protect me on the left side;
may Rakṣa Phaṭ Ugratāriṇī protect the back part of my head.
May the six-syllabled Kullukeśī, Vijayānandatāriṇī,
who holds a sword, a lotus, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, protect me always.
O wearer of jewels, wielder of the thunderbolt, Hrīṃ Hūṃ Trīṃ, O you who bring all under control!
O Pratisarā, protect, protect me! Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ, accompanied by Svāhā.
May the Goddess Śrī Maṇitāriṇī, residing in the topknot-knot (*śikhā-granthi*), protect me.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ kṣrauṃ! Drive away all obstacles, tear them asunder! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
May Vighnatārā protect me in all directions at all times. Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ āḥ surekhe hūṃ.
Vajrarekhe ṭhaḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! May Surekhogratāriṇī, who is pleased upon the earth, protect me.

Having thus assigned the eight *kullukā* mantras, the supreme practitioner should assign those eighty-four variations to the body at their respective locations. "Oṃ, may the five-syllabled one—she who is named Ekajaṭā, the goddess who removes dullness from the three worlds—protect my head with Hrīṃ Strīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ. Hrīṃ [is for] the two eyes.

May the blue goddess Trilocanā protect the woman with *strīṃ hūṃ*. May Bhīmatāriṇī protect the forehead with *śrīṃ hrīṃ strīṃ haṃ saḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. May Jñānatārā, who burns the fuel of ignorance, protect the space between the eyebrows eternally with *oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sahrīṃ sahuṃ phaṭ svāhā*. *Oṃ hrīṃ*.

HAṂSAḤ ŚRĪṂ HAṂ SAḤ STRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ ŚRĪṂ PRĀṆATĀRIṆĪ—may she who causes the destruction of all calamities protect me in the center of the nose. KLĪṂ HRĪṂ STRĪṂ HŪṂ OṂ KLĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ MOHANATĀRIṆĪ—may she who delivers from delusion protect me. In the lotus of the face, holding a goad and a lotus, with hands like lotuses granting boons and fearlessness—OṂ.

*Hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ*: May Lambauṣṭhī, the Enchantress of the Universe, protect my lips. *Āṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hūṃ hūṃ hasastrīṃ phaṭ ṭa*: May she always protect my lower lip. May the Goddess Anantatāriṇī, who bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation, protect me. *Aiṃ oṃ hūṃ aiṃ strīṃ hrīṃ ph hūṃ ai*: May Vāktāriṇī protect me.
May the supreme goddess Vākpradā, who bestows auspiciousness in speech, protect me. Oṃ tāre strīṃ mahātāre hūṃ tāriṇy ugratāriṇī! Protect, protect the world, O Tārā; hūṃ phaṭ! O Tāriṇī, protect me!
395) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jrīṃ strīṃ hrīṃ phaṭ e hrīṃ, speak, O bestower of the power of speech!

Omniscient One, command! *strīṃ* hūṃ! O Tārīṇī, protect my tongue! *aiṃ hrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ hasastrīṃ phaṭ*, O Caṇḍogrātārīṇī, may the Goddess who destroys fierce fear protect my chin! *oṃ kalahrīṃ hūṃ hasastrīṃ klīṃ klīṃ phaṭ*, O Kālatārīṇī!

May the fierce one, golden-hued and adorned with serpent-earrings, protect my cheeks: *oṃ yuṃ hūṃ hūṃ śrīṃ hasastrīṃ klīṃ hrīṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ aiṃ sadā*. May Mahāmāyā, the Vidyā Śrīśabdatāriṇī, protect my ears: *oṃ śrīṃ glauṃ gaṃ hūṃ hasastrīṃ aiṃ*.

May she who holds a pair of lotuses and the gestures of boon-granting and fearlessness, the Savior from Fear (*Abhayatāriṇī*), always protect my cheeks. Oṃ klīṃ kili kili strīṃ phaṭ—may the Excellent Savior (*Sutāriṇī*) protect my throat. Śrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ strīṃ clūṃ hasastrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ strīṃ hūṃ kṣeṃ hūṃ—O Karālinī, O Mahātārā, protect, protect!

HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ—[this mantra] protects the crown of the head (kakutsthala). OṂ JRĪṂ HRĪṂ STRĪṂ HŪṂ HAṂ SA-STRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ—Tāriṇī, protect the neck! OṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ TRĪṂ KLĪṂ HASA-STRĪṂ BHASTRĪṂ BHASTRĪṂ JAYE JAYE MOHOGRE PIṄGAJATE HRĪṂ STRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ—may [she] protect [me].

May the goddess Jayadatāriṇī protect my two shoulders. Oṃ hūṃ hrīṃ trīṃ hrīṃ drāṃ drīṃ kḷṃ haṃ saḥ aiṃ hūṃ phaṭ. May that Jayadatāriṇī always protect the roots of my arms. Oṃ drāṃ drīṃ dāvinī klinne drāvaya drāvaya drutaṃ sarvaśatrūn (Oṃ drāṃ drīṃ, O Dāvinī, O Klinne, cause all enemies to flee, cause them to flee quickly!).

O Mahāmāyā, O Great Deliverer! Hrīṃ sahrīṃ phaṭ svāhā! May Vidrāvatārī protect the middle of my arms. Oṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ bhamalavarayūṃ śrīṃ kṣrīṃ hūṃ sahrīṃ saḥ phaṭ! May Siddhitārā, the accomplisher of all aims, protect my two hands. Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ hūṃ.

*Ha-sa-strīṃ phaṭ*, she who destroys with her fingers; *Oṃ khphreṃ strīṃ hūṃ haṃ saḥ kṣrīṃ*, she who destroys by rending nails against nails; *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ drāṃ drīṃ hūṃ clūṃ strīṃ saḥ khphreṃ*, O Caṇḍayoginī, O Mistress of Yoga, O Great Tārā, O crusher of the Asura Tāraka, intoxicate the Pramathas!

Tear asunder my wicked enemies! Wither them! Rend them! *Kṣāṃ kṣrīṃ dhūṃ dhūṃ*! Bind them, bind them! Destroy all misfortune! *Strīṃ*! May Karālā Mahogratarīṇī, the wielder of the sword, who bestows the bliss of victory, protect me! *Oṃ strīṃ hūṃ yaralavasahūṃ*.

HASAKṢAMALAVARAYŪṂ HRĪṂ HRĪṂ OṂ—may Yoginī Tāriṇī protect my belly region. OṂ HRĪṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ STRĪṂ STRĪṂ SAḤ KLĪṂ KLĪṂ—O bestower of liberation! HAṂSAḤ KLĪṂ SAHRĪṂ—protect me on both sides, O Bhṛgutāriṇī, SVĀHĀ HAṂSAḤ. OṂ HRĪṂ STRĪṂ.
HŪṂ PHAṬ! I am that Mahogratārī; protect me, you who are close to my heart and strengthened by the power of life-force (prāṇa-śakti)! OṂ TĀRE TĀRAYA TRĪṂ HŪṂ HAṂSAḤ!
You who cause the protection of the three worlds—HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ! Protect my pair of breasts!

O bestower of victory! Oṃ kṣāṃ hūṃ kalahas-trīṃ phaṭ, she who wards off Kālarudra; protect, protect, hūṃ phaṭ aiṃ hūṃ, she who delivers the belly from Rudra. Oṃ hrīṃ bhastrī hasastrīṃ phaṭ, she who delivers my navel; hrīṃ klīṃ hūṃ sahas-trīṃ phaṭ, she who delivers the *liṅga* through procreation.

Oṃ hsauṃ hrīṃ hasastrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ klīṃ strīṃ phaṭ! May that Goddess, the supporter of the three worlds and the savior from worldly existence, always protect my support. Oṃ hūṃ hrīṃ strīṃ jambhini śrīṃ hrīṃ vaśini klīṃ mohini drāṃ drāviṇi! Strike down, drive away, delude, and agitate my enemies!

396) Agitate, *hūṃ hūṃ*! Quickly crush, crush! O *Tārā*, O *Tāriṇī*, O wearer of Rudra’s bones, O you whose form is Brahmā, O you who provide protection to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva! *kṣīṃ phaṭ*! O Mother, O protectress, O savior Goddess, may you always protect my three parts! *hūṃ hrīṃ strīṃ śrīṃ*!

*Hasastrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*: May she protect me. She whose hips are full and whose every limb is perfect, who always delivers all—*hrāṃ hūṃ hrīṃ klīṃ blūṃ strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ*: may she, the deliverer from brokenness, protect my thighs. *Oṃ jhrīṃ jrīṃ krīṃ hasastrīṃ phaṭ hūṃ hrīṃ*: paralyze and delude!

*Stambhaya drāvaya drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ clūṃ saḥ*, O Goddess Jambhakatāriṇī, paralyze and put to flight those belonging to the faction of my enemies; protect the pair of my knees! *Oṃ śrīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ jrīṃ jhrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ*, may she protect me; may that Great Goddess Bhramatāriṇī protect the pair of my shanks! *Oṃ*.
Hrīṃ gāṃ gīṃ glauṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ glauṃ hūṃ strīṃ phaṭ Parameśvarī!
May the Goddess Śrīgaṇatāriṇī always protect the pair of my ankles. Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ! May Parokṣatāriṇī protect the soles of my feet. Oṃ hūṃ hrīṃ phaṭ Mahātārā! May she protect the toes of my feet.

Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ glauṃ laṃ hasastrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhāsvarūpiṇī! May the Goddess Śrībhūmitāriṇī protect me eternally from beneath my feet. Oṃ kṣauṃ kṣīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ strīṃ hsauṃ phreṃ phaṭ īśvari! Turu turu strīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, O you who consist of the splendor of the vajra! Aiṃ.

Phaṭ! O you who ward off all missiles, weapons, and waters; O you who destroy all striking instruments; O you who avert all malevolent rites, sorcery, planetary influences, and misfortunes! Paralyze all missiles! Strīṃ! Crush! Hrīṃ! Tear asunder! Bhañjaya! Drāṃ! Bind! Klūṃ! Torment! Hsauṃ Hraḥ Phaṭ!

May the Mahogratāriṇī-vidyā protect the pores of my skin—the Goddess who holds all weapons in her hands and bestows fearlessness in every direction. Oṃ hrīṃ bhrūṃ trūṃ rūṃ vrūṃ hūṃ! Salutations, O Blessed One, fanged one, with a terrifying face, of most fierce form, Kālikā, you who are both playful and immovable, kluṃ kluṃ kluṃ!

O you with a tongue like lightning, hūṃ hūṃ! O you adorned with flesh from the hips and loins, wearer of a broad garland of severed heads, cause them to melt, cause them to melt! O Great Fierce One, you who wither the hearts of enemy warriors, elephants, and horses; you who steal away every gaze; you who cause the transformation of all weapons; you whose eyes are knit in a frown, you of uneven eyes!
O you whose limbs are smeared with great quantities of blood, fat, flesh, marrow, and grease;

O you who possess the colors of various clouds—kahakaha, mahamaha, bhrūṃda, and bhrūṃda; O you whose body is strewn with dripping bells; O you who delight in the flesh of corpses; O Bimbe, Bimbe, Raṇabimbe!

*Raudrarūpe hlauṃ hlauṃ hlaḥ kunta kunta ākarṣaya ākarṣaya dhunu dhunu heṃ haḥ khphreṃ vijṛmbhini hūṃ kṣauṃ namo jaya tryailokyavijaye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*— may Tārā Tryailokyavijayā always protect all my limbs. *Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ cāṃ*.

Cīṃ caiṃ hūṃ phaṭ śrīṃ hrīṃ Maheśvari hūṃ Vidyutprabhe Vidye, O giver of victory and bliss, protect me! Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ cāṃ cīṃ caiṃ hūṃ phaṭ śrīṃ hrīṃ Maheśvari hūṃ Vidyutprabhe Vidye, O bestower of the joy of victory, O Goddess consisting of consciousness and bliss, O sentient one!

"O Thou whose nature is consciousness, may Haṃsa, Haṃsā, Haṃsī, Hūṃ, and Saḥ protect Caitanyatāriṇī. Having thus performed the three-fold pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*), one should install the eight supports (*ādhāra*) with the syllables consisting of Śiva and Śakti, conjoined with the mantra of Tāriṇī: Oṃ Hrīṃ Strīṃ Ḍāṃ Ḍīṃ.
Ḍūṃ ḍaiṃ ḍaḥ ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-ha-iṃ hūṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ glau!
O Ḍākinī Tāriṇī, whose essence is the element of earth, together with Kālāgnirudra, may you always protect my support!
Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasakhaphreṃ hsauṃ ya-ra-la-va-sa-hūṃ hsauṃ hasakhaphreṃ.
Śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ, O dweller in the *ādhāra*, together with Kālāgnirudra, protect, protect my *ādhāra*, svāhā!
(397) Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ raiṃ rauṃ raḥ strīṃ raḍalakasahaiṃ aiṃ.

Hrīṃ śrīṃ hasakhaphreṃ strīṃ lavarayūṃ hsauḥ saḥ phaṭ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ vaṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ. O Thou who reignest, O Refuge of Water, together with Brahmā, protect the foundation; O Thou who art composed of the universe, cut through my water-born obstacles! Protect me, O Rākini, O Tāriṇī! Oṃ strīṃ.

hrīṃ lāṃ līṃ lūṃ laiṃ lauṃ laḥ phaṭ hsauḥ saḥ phaṭ laḍarakasahauṃ hraiṃ hraḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sahakhaphreṃ hsauḥ hasakṣamalavarayūṃ hsauḥ hasakhaphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ

Phaṃ! O Sāttvikī, whose form is the individual soul (jīvātman); Śrīṃ Hrīṃ! O Bestower of Rudra-bliss; O Maheśvarī, composed of splendor, blazing with the fire of cosmic destruction; O Goddess Lākini, O Savior! Always protect the Maṇipūra [cakra]. Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ Kaiṃ Kauṃ Kaḥ Strīṃ Hsauṃ Saḥ Klīṃ Kalaraḍarasahauṃ.

HŪṂ ŚRĪṂ AIṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ HASAKHAPHREṂ HSAUṂ HSAUṂ HASAKṢAMALAVARAYŪṂ HSAUṂ HASAKHAPHREṂ ŚRĪṂ HRĪṂ AIṂ KAṂ KHAṂ GAṂ GHAṂ ṄAṂ CAṂ CHAṂ JAṂ JHAṂ ÑAṂ ṬAṂ ṬHAṂ PHAṬ! O Goddess, whose essence is the supreme reality (paratattva), who brings about consciousness to the universe!

O Lotus-dweller, residing on the chest of Viṣṇu; O Goddess Kamalālayā, the syllable *klīṃ*, the goddess Kāmadā, who awakens the power of the vital breath (*prāṇaśakti*); O Goddess Kākini, O Savior (*tāriṇī*), protect the Unstruck (*anāhata*) forever! *oṃ hrīṃ trīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hauṃ hraiṃ strīṃ hsauḥ phaṭ* O Supreme and Inferior One (*parāpare*), *sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ saiṃ*.
Sauṃ saḥ hrīṃ saḥ saḍaralakahauṃ hraṃ hraṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasakhapreṃ hsauṃ kṣamalavarayūṃ hsauṃ hasakhaphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ phaṭ parāparāpare aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ.
Phaṭ! O Goddess whose nature is space, O Vidyunmatī, O Virocanā, O Goddess who is the refuge of Hiraṇyagarbha, glauḥ hūṃ!
Protect me always with purity! O Goddess who resembles a fierce maṇḍala, O Sākini, O Tāriṇī! Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ phaṭ śrīṃ hasakalaraḍaiṃ aiṃ.

Hrīṃ śrīṃ hasakhaphreṃ lhauḥ hrīḥ trīṃ phaṭ ṭhaṃ ṭhaḥ sphura sphura lava prakṣa sahasrīṃ hsauṃ hasakhaphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ haṃ kṣaṃ haṃ saḥ hūṃ sohaṃ hrīṃ phaṭ! O you who consist of mind, O abode of the Brahma-Tārā, O Sovereign, eternally residing in the heart of Sadāśiva!

O Hākinī, O Tāriṇī, always protect my longing mind! Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ haṃ yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ yaiṃ yauṃ yaḥ sauṃ haṃ haṃ sīṃ strīṃ hsauṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ hasakhaphreṃ hsauṃ! O Blessed One, O Mother consisting of consciousness, whose essence is the principle of intellect (buddhitattva)!
*Hasakṣamalavarayūṃ hasakṣamalavarayīṃ hsauṃ sahakhaphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ*.

O Goddess who consists of wisdom, who pervades the universe, whose form is the entire phenomenal world, *haṃsaḥ sohaṃ hsauṃ saḥ phaṭ*, O Goddess whose essence is the reality of the world, may this single petal protect me! *Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ*.
O Mother of the World, O Bestower of Joy to the World! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ strīṃ phaṭ!
O Thou whose form is the delight of the world! May the syllable *hrīṃ*, who is the nature of Being-Consciousness, protect my principle of ego (*ahaṃtattva*).
Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasakhaphra hrīṃ hūṃ klīṃ saḥ hsauṃ strīṃ phaṭ! O Thou of Non-Terrible Face!

Tāre hūṃ, O you who bring about all confidence! Hsauṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hasakhaphreṃ saklīṃ hūṃ śrīṃ hsauṃ hrīṃ aiṃ saḥ, O you who are presided over by the thousand-spoked [wheel]! Hūṃ hrīṃ, O you who are adorned by Mahāśiva! Protect, protect my ego-sense, O Tāriṇī, the consciousness of the universe! Oṃ hrīṃ.

HŪṂ STRĪṂ HASA-STRĪṂ HASAKALAHRĪṂ HSAUṂ TĀRIṆI BRAHMA-TĀRIṆI HSAUṂ HASAKHPHREṂ HŚRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ HRĪṂ AIṂ PARAME PARAME PARE GHORE GHORE MAHĀGHORE AGHORE GHORARŪPIṆI GHORAGHORATARE BHASRĀṂ BHASRĪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ PARAMEŚVARĪ.

O Ugratāriṇī, who carries one across to the supreme Brahman of consciousness and bliss; Śrīṃ Saḥ Hrīṃ Saḥ Phaṭ! O You who rest upon the pure lotus seat on the couch of Supreme Śiva, O You who are exceedingly tender with innate bliss, protect me!
(398) Having duly assigned the nine Tārās, one should again assign the six limbs: Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ Oṃ.

*Hasastrīṃ hruṃ hrīṃ strīṃ phaṭ svāhā*. May she protect the heart! She is Bhairavatāriṇī, bearing the sword, the lotus, the boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness. *Aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ īṃ aiṃ kalahrīṃ hasakalahrīṃ saklīṃ klīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*.

*Mātaṅginī Mohinī hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ aiṃ Vajravairocanīye hūṃ hūṃ aiṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! O Goddess Khaḍgogratārā, may you protect my head with hrīṃ!* *Oṃ īṃ aiṃ ka la hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ śrīṃ ha sa ka la hrīṃ sa hūṃ hrīṃ! Protect my crown-lock (śikhā) with this!*

O *Tāriṇī* who delivers me across the three cities, *hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ trīṃ aiṃ*, O *Vajravairocanī*, *hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. O *Vajratārā*, make my limbs adamantine (*vajra*). Protect all my limbs with armor, O glorious *Vajratāriṇī*. *Oṃ hūṃ hrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ namaḥ*.
O Sovereign who delivers from the state of being an outcaste! O you who delight the faces of all! Śrīṃ! O you who bring all beings under control! Strīṃ!

O you who bring all women and men under control! O you who bring all enemies under control! Hrīṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Hastrīṃ! O you who bring all kings under control! O you who bring all the wicked under control! Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ! [Salutation] to the circle of the eyes.

O Tārā, ever-abiding Mother Maṅgī, enchantress of the universe, protect me! Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hsauḥ strīṃ hraḥ phaṭ strīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ oṃ Kāli Kāli oṃ oṃ oṃ hraḥ strīṃ hūṃ khapreṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ stryauṃ stryaḥ sahai.

Haṃ saḥ! Homage to the Blessed Lady, O Pracaṇḍabālikā, wielder of the sword, trident, and mace; hūṃ hūṃ hreṃ hraiṃ! O bearer of all powers, destroyer of all enemies, eater of blood and flesh, O Terrible One, holder of the skull-topped staff and the khaṭvāṅga! Protect me, protect me, O Vijayā! Destroy my enemies!
Destroy all the wicked; ward off misfortunes;
slay the fear of all grahas, yakṣas, bhūtas, and cruel mātṛs; O Kuṣmāṇḍa, Bhairava, Kṣetrapāla, ward off and ward off the ḍākinīs, uraṅgamas, and the sky-dwelling brahmarākṣasas who [threaten] me!
O Blazing One! *Hūṃ*! Strike down those who openly or secretly commit acts of sorcery and malice against me;
lead them to destruction, lead them there! Crush them, crush them! Annihilate them, annihilate them!
Dry them up, dry them up! *Bhrūṃ Rūṃ Kṣrīṃ Kṣrauṃ Bhraiṃ Phaṭ*! [This is] the mantra of Kālikā for both hands.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*), one should perform the pervasive projection (*vyāpaka*) with the *Gāyatrī*: *Hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ ekajaṭe vidmahe | Hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ pare nīle vikaṭadaṃṣṭre hrīṃ dhīmahi | Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ aiṃ saḥ strīṃ tannastāre pracodayāt māṃ pāhyugratāriṇi | Oṃ Akṣobhyaḥ.*

May the agitator protect my head at all times. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Māṃ! May Rocana protect me always in the east. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ! May Siddhināyaka protect me always in the west. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! May Nāmaka always protect me in the southeast. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ...

HŪṂ PHAṬ! May Māmaka protect me always in the southwest (Nairṛtya). AIṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ! May Pāvaka protect me always in the northwest (Vāyavya). AIṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ! May Tāraka protect me always in the northeast (Aiśānī). Outside of that, in the eastern direction, [may] AIṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ OṂ NAMO [protect me].
Homage! O Brahmāṇī, protect, protect! O rider of the swan, O Haṃsinī! Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Hrīṃ Hsaiṃ Strīṃ Saḥ!
O you who are served by Asitāṅga, protect, protect! O Mahāmāyā! Haṃsaḥ! She whose nature is the syllable *so'ham* (I am He)!
In the south-eastern direction: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrauṃ Strīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Īṃ Hrīṃ! Homage, homage!
O Māheśvarī, mounted upon the bull, holding a trident in hand, grant me fearlessness! Heṃ Hauṃ Hūṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ!
Protect, protect me, O you who are adorned by Rurubhairava! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Strīṃ Aiṃ!
Salutations, O Blessed One! Hrīṃ Hrīṃ! O Kaumārī, protect, protect me from the south, O you whose vehicle is the peacock!

In the hand of Śakti: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Hraiṃ 399) O you adorned by Caṇḍabhairava! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Oṃ Glauṃ! Salutations, O Blessed One! O Vārāhī, protect me, protect me with your tusk-weapon, O you of great strength!

O Vidyā accompanied by Unmatta, protect me always in the southwest! Aiṃ hrīṃ hūṃ oṃ klīṃ haiṃ haṃ saḥ so'haṃ namo namaḥ bhagavati vaiṣṇavi śrīṃ hrīṃ trīṃ O you who are borne by Garuḍa, O you whose weapon is the discus, protect me, protect me! Aiṃ jauṃ hauṃ haṃ sauḥ saḥ phaṭ.
O Goddess who revolves through a thousand illusions, O Krodhabhairava and Bhairavī, protect us in the western direction, O Queen of Devas;

ward off all obstacles! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Drīṃ Trīṃ Hsraiṃ Aiṃ Trāṃ Īṃ Ūṃ Hrīṃ! Salutations, salutations to the Blessed One, the Invincible Aindri, seated upon the king of elephants, holding a vajra in her hand!
HAIṂ HSAUṂ! O destroyer of my enemies, together with Kapālin, protect me always in the northwestern direction!
AIṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ OṂ STRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ! CĀṂ CĪṂ CAIṂ! Salutations, O Blessed One, O Śrī Cāmuṇḍā, who dwells upon the chest of a corpse, who bears the khaṭvāṅga as your weapon, HRAUṂ HRĪṂ HSAUṂ!

O Bhīṣaṇā, in the north, protect me always! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ūṃ Īṃ Laṃ Hrīṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Srīṃ Strīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Salutations, salutations to the Blessed One, Mahālakṣmī, seated upon the lotus throne, supreme wielder of the lotus weapon! Oṃ Hrīṃ Hklīṃ Hklauṃ Hsaiṃ Hastrīṃ.

O source of prosperity, O bliss of the Bhairava of withdrawal, protect me always in the northeast! Aiṃ Haiṃ Hauṃ! May Hetuka protect me in the east! Aiṃ Vaṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Hrauṃ Slauṃ Saḥ Phaṭ! May Tripurāntaka protect me in the southeast! Klauṃ Hūṃ! May Vahnivetāla protect me from fear in the south! Aiṃ Vaṃ!

May Agnijihva protect [me] in the south; Aiṃ Aṃ Kaṃ. May Nairṛta protect me; Hūṃ Hrīṃ Kreṃ Īṃ Kāṃ Bhrūṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ. May Kālākṣa always protect me. In the northwest (Vāyukoṇa), Aiṃ Maṃ Hūṃ; may Mataya Bhairava protect [me]. In the north (Udīcī), Eṃ Aiṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ; may Ekapāda always protect [me], Aiṃ.
May Bhīmā protect me; may Bhīmavaṭuka always protect me from the northeast. Oṃ tāre tāre mahātāre uttāre bhayatāriṇī! Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jrīṃ hūṃ kroṃ vaṃ kroṃ laṃ!
Crush, crush the vajra-stones and weapons! Make them flee! Hrīṃ haḥ kahakaha vimoḍaya!

Vimoḍaya hasastrīṃ phaṭ svāhā! O Tāriṇī, protect me from the weapon of Indra! Oṃ tāre vaṃ viśvatāre hrīṃ strīṃ! O Tāriṇī of Varuṇa, vaṃ kroṃ vaṃ kroṃ! Paralyze the weapons of Agni; cause them to flee quickly; turn them back; cut them down swiftly; whirl the weapon about; rend it asunder; contract it!

Cut down all enemies; for my destruction, protect me from the fire-weapon, O you who cross over the obstruction of fire! Oṃ hrīṃ tāre mahātāre kāladaṇḍavināśini hūṃ kroṃ yaṃ kroṃ hasakroṃ phaṭ! Ward off the staff-weapons, shatter them, tear them apart, and crush them!

Cut, cut! Rend the weapon! Paralyze, paralyze! *Kṣrīṃ Hrīṃ*! O Tāriṇī, protect me from the weapon of Yama! *Oṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Trīṃ*, O Viṣṇu-Tārā, O destroyer of all Asuras, ward off all the weapons of the Asuras! Rend them, shatter them, crush them, break them, grind them down, destroy them, strike at the enemy! Druh!

From all the incitements of the asuras: ĀḤ! O divine line, divine line, HŪṂ! O diamond-line, O rending one! KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢUṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ HSAUḤ! Destroy the malice of sorcery; tear asunder the array of illusion! TRĪṂ! O terrifying one, protect me from the weapons of the asuras, O Sovereign! OṂ HRĪṂ TRĪṂ HŪṂ.

Mahātāra hraṃ hraḥ kroṃ vaṃ kroṃ vaṃ kroṃ kṣūṃ kṣauṃ vaṣaṭ! Blaze, blaze, O wielder of the trident! Kṣrīṃ! O remover of the fear of evil planets, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Ward off the Varuṇa-weapon, the sorcery, and the malice; dry up, agitate, kṣycaṃ phaṭ! Split, split! Destroy, O Āpyadurgā!
O Durgā, protect me from calamities in this difficult and perilous place—phaṭ svāhā! May she who is the glorious Deliverer from Durga protect me in the west.
400) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! She who is to be known as Bhīmatārā, who dwells upon the king of mountains;

she of great fangs, great speed, great fortitude, and great strength—hrāṃ hrāṃ sthāṃ sthīṃ! O Mahocchuṣmā, destroy the musical instruments and weapons! Dhūṃ dhūṃ! O Dhūmāvatī, O Wet One (Klinne), moisten [them]!
O Vajratārī, who causes the unrighteous to flee, scatter the enemy's winds and weapons! Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ vajravairocanīye vajratāriṇī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Hraiṃ saklīṃ, pulverize and shatter the mace;
destroy the weapons of the yakṣas and the illusions of the yakṣas! Drīṃ, cause them to flee! Drīṃ, release [me from them]!

Protect me in the north, O Goddess, on all sides, O Vajratāriṇī! Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ klīṃ strīṃ, O you whose essential nature is the power-principle (śakti-tattva) of Kālarudra; hraiṃ hrauṃ kṣrauṃ, O Mahātārā, O Tāriṇī, O you whose nature is Brahman; O Pracaṇḍā, shatter the weapons of the Pramathas! Hrīṃ haḥ, destroy them!

Drive away and ward off the fierce performers of cruel deeds, the violent Pramathas, serpents, Rākṣasas, Brahmarākṣasas, and Vetālas; O Pracaṇḍatāriṇī, protect me always from the weapons of Rudra! Oṃ hrīṃ haṃ saḥ kroṃ oṃ haṃsaḥ chrāṃ sohaṃ kroṃ vaṣaṭ.

HKLĪṂ SAKLĪṂ HASAKLĪṂ PHAṬ HŪṂ STRĪṂ! O Brahmogratāriṇī, quickly bring the Brahma-missiles to pacification; O Śivā, the soul of the universe! All rites declared in the Vedas that yield the fruit of sorcery and malice—may they destroy those very people who perform them against me!
The destroyers, overcome by the fire of wrath out of fear of the wheel of Pracaṇḍatāriṇī— Oṃ Hrīṃ Strīṃ Hūṃ Hasastrīṃ Hrīṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaiṃ Gauṃ Gaḥ Saḥ Phaṭ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ.
HŪṂ SLŪṂ SUPARṆE KROṂ AMBĀNTĀṂ SAHAUṂ HSAUḤ HAṂSAḤ SOHAṂ!
Strike down the arrows of the *nāgas*, strike them down completely! DRĀṂ DRĪṂ HRĪṂ CLŪṂ STRĪṂ HASASTRĪṂ KHAIṂ KHAIṂ KṢAḤ!
O Tārkṣya-Tāriṇī, [protect us from] the weapons of poison and snakes!
"O Goddess Śrītārkṣyatāriṇī, come and destroy the serpent-nooses and all weapons that cause fear!
Having thus repelled the enemy's fortress of missiles, one of pure intellect should recite this great mantra, which destroys all fears: oṃ hsauṃ vasahūṃ kalahrīṃ hasastrīṃ phaṭ

O Mahākaulinī, adorned with ornaments of garlands of human entrails; O Mahābrahmavādinī, who causes the intoxication of great wealth; O bestower of great enjoyments: make our body adamantine, *kuru kuru*;
slay the wicked ones, *hana hana*; agitate the rulers of the earth, *kṣobhaya kṣobhaya*; shatter the enemy's army!
BHAÑJAYA JAYAṄKARI GAGANAGĀMINI YAMALAVARAYŪṂ HAYAMALAVARAYŪṂ BHAMALAVARAYŪṂ ŚAMALAVARAYŪṂ KṢAMALAVARAYŪṂ BHAMALAVARAYŪṂ HASAKṢAMALAVARAYŪṂ SAHASAKṢAMALAVARAYŪṂ HAṂSAḤ SOHAṂ HŪṂ HRĪṂ STRĪṂ.

Hsauṃ drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ trāṃ trīṃ trūṃ tryaiṃ trauṃ traḥ | O Śrīmatkullukatāriṇī, protect me, protect me everywhere, svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ | O Mahādevī, mounted upon a horse, bestower of victory, may you eternally protect my vehicles!
The accomplisher of all aims: *hrīṃ hraiṃ surekhe devi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. May the chariot protect me!

*rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ raiṃ rauṃ raḥ rakṣiṇi hūṃ phaṭ paramānandatāriṇi*. *Oṃ hūṃ*, to the one worthy of the King of Puṣpaketu, who has gone and returned, who has perfectly arisen, and who is accompanied by the planets, zodiac signs, and constellations.

To her who dwells within the orb of the risen sun, who is ever-arisen as pure consciousness, *hrīṃ trīṃ*, to the Star of the Supreme Light, *hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. *Hrīṃ*, O Jyotistāriṇī, you who are moist and dripping with moisture, always protect, protect my banner;
destroy the factions of my enemies; salutations be unto you! *Oṃ klīṃ*, may Kāmākarṣiṇī protect me!

The accomplisher of all aims, the attractor of splendor, the attractor of intellect, the attractor of knowledge, the goddess who attracts the mind, she whose form attracts delusion, the attractor of asceticism; 401) the attractor of weapons, the attractor of spirits, the attractor of vehicles, the attractor of mantras.

She who attracts the field, she whose form is the attraction of the difficult-to-attain, and she whose form is the attraction of jewels; she who attracts the ego, and she whose form is the attraction of yoga; she whose form is the attraction of knowledge, and she whose form is the attraction of faith;
she who attracts vital energy (*ojas*), as well as the paralyzer, the deluder, the liquefier, and the agitator.

She who takes the form of a magnetizing charm, the attractor, the deluder, the supreme mistress of the five arrows, the embodiment of all forms—may Mahātārā protect me always in battle. With hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness and holding a lotus, may Ugratāriṇī protect me in the forest, in the terrifying wilderness, in the supportless void, and upon the flood of waters. In adversity, in terrible distress, and in the desolate desert—may she protect me.
In her mountain abode, may the Goddess who wields the sword and lotus, the deliverer from distress, protect me.

In the forest teeming with lions and tigers, a terrifying abode, may she of the fearsome fangs, bearing a sword and a skull-bowl, protect me eternally. In the assembly hall during a debate on the scriptures, amidst a throng of enemies, may Nīlasarasvatī, her hand clenched in a fist, protect me. She is short and stands in the *pratyālīḍha* posture.
Seated upon a corpse, the goddess Śivā, with her hands in the fist-gesture, is remembered as one who instantly paralyzes all beings.

May the Goddess who carries one across to immortality, whose lotus-face has a gentle smile and dripping buds of nectar, protect me constantly from diseases. O Goddess, protect me everywhere from the Pramathas, Piśācas, Rākṣasas, and even from Grahas,
as well as from Brahmarākṣasas, Vetālas, Kuṣmāṇḍas, and the like.
From Siṃhāsya comes Bhūtatāriṇī. Oṃ! In the eastern direction, in the southeast, the south, and likewise in the southwest.

May the Goddess Ugratāriṇī, who holds a sword and shield, protect me in the directions of Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Raudra, and Gaurava, as well as in all vulnerable positions and openings in due order. May she protect my armies and my mounts, such as elephants, horses, and the like— may the Goddess Ugrāpattāriṇī protect them.
Bestower of all auspiciousness, protect my lineage, my friends, and my affectionate wives.

May Mahogratāriṇī, the destroyer of all fears, protect [me]. Oṃ! Hail to you, Ugratārā, born from the seed-syllable *Hūṃ*, with a flickering tongue, O terrifying one, fierce wielder of the knife and the chisel! O Tārā, whose abode is the sky, the three-syllabled one, expounder of Brahman, the purifier of the perfected ones (*siddhas*), pure one—salutations to you, O Ugratāriṇī!

Protect me everywhere from all fears, O Goddess Ugratārā! By the grace of Ugratārā, let no harm-doers injure me. Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ hasastrīṃ sphura sphura hasastrīṃ phaṭ prasphura prasphura strīṃ hrīṃ caṭa caṭa hūṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ.

HASAKALARĪṂ PRACAṬA PRACAṬA HŪṂ HRĪṂ KAHA KAHA KṢRĪṂ KṢĪṂ KROṂ HŪṂ VAMA VAMA STRĪṂ HŪṂ ME RIPŪN GHĀTAYA GHĀTAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ KLĪṂ KROṂ ṬHAḤ KṢRĪṂ SAḤ HASAKṢAMALAVARAYŪṂ HASAKṢAMALAVARAYĪṂ HASAKHPHREṂ HSAUṂ SAHŪṂ.

Haṃsaḥ so’haṃ hūṃ phaṭ so’haṃ—may Tāriṇī protect all my limbs! May Nityā, the awakener of all mantras, protect me at all times! [And may] Bhairavī, Sundarī, Kālī, Mātaṅgī, and Chinnamastakā [protect me].

And Nīlasarasvatī—thus the sixfold mantra has been proclaimed. Thus it has been told to you, O child, that which is difficult even for the gods to obtain. Named Tryailokyavijaya, it is the singular embodiment of the Brahma-mantra. Having become armored with this, and meditating upon Ugratāriṇī—the Supreme Power (Parā Śakti) residing in the foundation (ādhāra)—having drawn her upward by contraction...

With effort, having closed [the eyes] at the crown of the head in supreme bliss (*parānanda*), meditate upon the splendor born of innate bliss (*sahajānanda*) as non-different from yourself. "I am Śiva, I am Bhairava, I am eternal bliss, I am the imperishable;
I am indeed the destroyer of enemies, for I am Mahogratāriṇī, consisting of all powers. 402) Sarvaśaktimayo...
"I am of the nature of Brahman, consisting of Tāriṇī"—contemplating yourself thus, apply the mantras without hesitation.

Remembering the Brahma-mantra, [the mantras] become radiant with the splendor of the mantra, O Brahmin, becoming indeed dense like dry wood in a fire. Having encased [the mantra] within the Brahma-mantras, one who recites the Tārikā mantra—

Or, by means of this armor-mantra (*kavaca*) of the *Tārikā*, his success will certainly be attained: Oṃ klīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ sakalahrīṃ strīṃ aiṃ kroṃ hrīṃ hūṃ Śrīmadekajaṭe brahmaṣoḍaśīsvarūpiṇi tripurasundari hrīṃ trīṃ hūṃ phaṭ ka e.
*Ī la hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ nīlasarasvati mahātāre sarvasiddhiṃ prayaccha oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ lauṃ strīṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Now, the yantra.
